Title: No eye-witnesses when Zara fell, Coroner's Court hears
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: There were no eye-witnesses when Zara Qairina Mahathir fell from the 3rd floor of her school hostel on July 16, 2025. the Coroner's Court was told.
The investigating officer, Inspector Wong Yew Zhung, said no one, including security guards or hostel wardens, had patrolled the third floor of the hostel block where Zara Qairina stayed on the night of the incident.
"My inspection also found that there were no closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in the hostel area that could have provided footage of the incident," he said while reading his written statement before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
Wong said statements from students indicated that Zara Qairina was last seen by a group of students at about 10pm on July 15 when she was summoned by several Form Four students over an alleged theft.
"Later that night, between 10.15pm and 10.30pm, several students from dormitory A-3-5 said they saw Zara enter the dormitory crying before lying down on the floor," he said.
Wong said that at about midnight on July 16, four Form One students in dormitory A-3-5 said Zara approached them and asked to borrow a pair of scissors, but they refused her.
Between 12.10am and 12.30am, three other Form One students said they saw Zara climbing a toilet partition wall on the third floor and looking towards them.
"At about 2.35am, a student who had woken up early to bathe said she went to the third-floor toilet and found the door of the first cubicle closed.
"When she tried to open it, someone inside pushed against the door. The person was wearing a sports shirt bearing the word 'Hanafi'.
"She could not see the person's face but said the shirt was similar to the one Zara was wearing when she was found unconscious," he said.
Zara was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school hostel building on July 16, 2025.
She was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
Her body was exhumed on August 9, 2025, for a post-mortem examination at the hospital's Forensic Medicine Department.
On August 20, 2025, five minors, identified by the pseudonyms Students A, B, C, D and E, were charged in the Children's Court with uttering insulting words at Zara Qairina. All pleaded not guilty.
The inquest began on September 3, 2025, to determine the cause and circumstances leading to Zara Qairina's death, including whether any criminal elements were involved.

Title: Man seeking loan to help family ends up as account mule
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man who sought a loan to help pay for his mother and sister's cancer treatment said he was under immense pressure after becoming an account mule.
Clerk Mohd Izzuddin Juppri, 38, claimed he became an account mule after seeking a RM10,000 loan in February 2020 to cover treatment costs for his mother and sister, both of whom were diagnosed with breast cancer.
He said the lender required him to surrender his bank card as a condition for securing the loan.
Izzuddin said he never received the money and decided to block his bank account a month later, only to discover five suspicious transactions.
"Four transactions involved licensed moneylending scams, while another involved a car sale.
"Three cases have been resolved, while two remain pending action by the authorities. My account has been frozen by the authorities, and I cannot open a new one.
"I hope the remaining cases can be resolved soon and, if possible, the investigations coordinated. I hope to open a new account afterwards," he said, adding that his sister died in March.
He was speaking at a press conference with the Malaysian International Humanitarian Organisation (MHO), which submitted an appeal to Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail at Bukit Aman yesterday, calling for authorities to consolidate related cases and conduct comprehensive investigations.
Another victim, who wished to be known only as Amy, 43, claimed she was also caught up in the scheme after taking a RM5,000 loan last year to ease her husband's financial burden amid the high cost of living in the capital.
However, she said her attempt to help her family turned into a nightmare when the bank card she surrendered was used for account mule activities, resulting in her being implicated in five cases.
She was also detained in a lock-up in Perak and subsequently suffered panic attacks.
"I have four cases in Perak, Pahang, Negri Sembilan and Kuala Lumpur, and another in Batu Pahat, Johor.
"I have had to spend money to attend court proceedings and visit police stations in different locations.
"This has changed my life, including my relationship with my husband, as we argue frequently. I sincerely hope the authorities can help us," she said.
MHO secretary-general Datuk Hishamuddin Hashim said the organisation was representing 24 account mule victims who were deceived and exploited, resulting in their bank accounts being used for transactions linked to scams and commercial crimes.
He said they were appealing to the Inspector-General of Police to review and coordinate related cases comprehensively to ensure justice for all parties.
"MHO hopes a comprehensive and coordinated review can identify links between police reports, prevent overlapping investigations and help authorities track down the masterminds behind the scams.
"We want firm action against the actual scammers, while those who may have been deceived or exploited should not continue to bear severe consequences without a fair assessment of the facts, their knowledge and their actual involvement," he said.

Title: Mexican man run over by ICE agents 'intentionally': Lawyer
Article:
HOUSTON: Federal immigration agents in an unmarked SUV ran over a Mexican man during a pursuit in Texas, breaking his right leg in three places, his lawyer said Monday.
On Saturday, 48-year-old construction worker Miguel Parra was on his way to work when he was struck during an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operation in Houston, Texas.
Surveillance video captured the moment when the dark SUV caught up with Parra, who was fleeing his vehicle on foot, and ran over him.
ICE officals told Houston Public Media that Parra "ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck."
Parra's lawyer Kim Bruno challenged that characterisation, telling reporters: "What happened is not an accident, it is something (done) intentionally and that is abuse."
ICE said they we seeking to detain Parra's passenger, who had a criminal record.
The incident marks the latest injuries sustained in the harsh national crackdown on immigration in the United States.
Cesar Espinosa, director of immigrant rights group FIEL Houston, said Parra has undergone surgery for his leg.
"He has an injury on his hip, a little below his knee and his ankle is fractured," Espinosa said. "He still has multiple surgeries to go" to "reconstruct his leg."
Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare previously led the vehicular crimes division, and said his office will investigate the Saturday wreck as a potential crime of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
"Multiple investigators who have decades of experience investigating auto-pedestrian crashes have all watched the surveillance, seen the scene and believe it is not an accidental strike," Teare told the Houston Chronicle.
The incident comes two days after Dominican national Oscar Belgal, 28, was shot and wounded by an ICE agent in New York while he was in a car with a five-year-old child. Authorities said he has a criminal record.
Last month, Venezuelan national Wilber Garces was shot in the back by an ICE agent while he was working as a delivery driver in Austin, Texas. The Department of Homeland Security accuses him of trying to run an agent over with his car.
In July, another ICE agent shot and killed Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado. Eyewitness accounts there dispute the official's accusation that he was attempting to run over an officer.
US President Donald Trump campaigned on tough immigration policies, but violent enforcement actions have drawn protests and criticism from all over the country.--REUTERS

Title: HLIB keeps 'Buy' call on MN Holdings, RM4.65 target
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its "Buy" call on MN Holdings Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM4.65, citing the company's strong positioning to benefit from Malaysia's accelerating power infrastructure investment cycle.
The investment bank said MN Holdings' latest contract win to build power facilities for a data centre brought its year-to-date contract win for 2027 to RM643 million, representing 64 per cent of HLIB's RM1 billion full-year target for the company.
Including the latest award, HLIB estimated MN Holdings' outstanding order book at a record RM1.89 billion, with data centre-related jobs accounting for the majority at 68 per cent.
"We remain positive on Malaysia's power infrastructure upcycle, with strong data centre and solar project pipelines driving demand for power infrastructure works from both private players and Tenaga.
"We continue to see MN Holdings as a key beneficiary of this upcycle, backed by its strong balance sheet and proven execution track record," it said in a note.
The firm said there is a potential for MN Holdings contract wins for financial year 2027 (FY27) to surpass RM1 billion.
HLIB added that Malaysia's power infrastructure cycle is set to accelerate in FY27; in particular, the additional five gigawatts of capacity approved by the Data Centre Task Force points to a significant pickup in project call-ups over 2027 through 2028.
"To meet the growing demand, Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) remains committed to its regulated capex plan, with spending expected to pick up further in FY27.
"Even before the anticipated acceleration, MN Holdings tenderbook has already reached RM4.7 billion, with TNB, data centre and solar tenders all at record highs.
"Within the data centre segment, we understand that several of MN Holdings' existing customers are expanding across multiple sites, which should translate into more project opportunities as each campus enters subsequent development phases," added HLIB.

Title: Zara's mother refused post-mortem, investigating officer tells inquest
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The late Zara Qairina Mahathir's mother refused to allow a post-mortem examination despite receiving an explanation from police, the investigating officer told the Coroner's Court.
Inspector Wong Yew Zhung said he met Noraidah Lamat at Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH) on July 17, 2025, after Zara Qairina, 13, was pronounced dead.
The 83rd witness said he received a call from Dr Pavankumar Balachandran informing him that Zara Qairina had died from "severe traumatic brain injury with hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy."
After the call, Wong and the duty photographer rushed to QEH where they met Dr Pavankumar and Noraidah in the neurosurgical ward.
"I informed and explained to Zara's mother that a post-mortem examination would be conducted to assist the investigation into her death.
"However, Zara's mother, refused to allow the post-mortem examination.
"I explained the post-mortem examination to her again, but she remained adamant, saying: 'No. I want to bury her immediately,'" he said before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
Wong said no POL 61 form, a police request for a post-mortem examination, was issued at the time because Noraidah had refused the procedure and Zara Qairina's cause of death had been established.
He said Noraidah also signed several documents on July 17, 2025, before the teenager's remains were released to her family for burial.
Among the documents was a Declaration of Voluntary Refusal of Post-Mortem Examination, where Noraidah acknowledged she did not wish for a post-mortem to be conducted, did not suspect any criminal act in connection with her daughter's death and would not request a post-mortem report from the hospital for medico-legal, insurance or other claims.
The other two documents were a Death Notification and Body Management Form and a Declaration of Confirmation of Funeral Arrangements.
Wong, however, said he applied for an order to exhume Zara Qairina's body on August 9, 2025, following instructions from the Attorney-General's Chambers.
Wong and a team from the Papar district police headquarters (IPD), assisted by the Sabah police contingent (IPK), proceeded to the Tanjung Ubi Muslim Cemetery in Kampung Mesapol Lama, Sipitang.
The exhumation was completed that night. Zara Qairina's was then taken to the Forensic Department at QEH for a post-mortem examination.
Wong said the examination began at 11am on August 10, 2025, led by forensic pathologist Dr Jessie Hiu, assisted by three other doctors - Dr Khairul Anuar Zainun, Dr Muhammad Uzair Ahmad Suriani and Dr Lau Cheng Cheng.
"Also present during the procedure were Papar criminal investigation division chief Assistant Superintendent Rosli Rasi, myself, Inspector Desmond Tanggapan, Zara's mother and her legal representative, Shahlan Jufri," he said.
Based on the post-mortem findings, Dr Jessie concluded that Zara Qairina's cause of death was severe traumatic brain injury with hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy.
"The cause of death determined by Dr Jessie following the post-mortem examination was the same as that confirmed on July 17.
"Dr Jessie's examination of the injuries found on Zara's body also showed that they were consistent with injuries sustained from a fall from height," he said.
Noraidah, who completed her testimony yesterday, attended today's proceedings and sat in the public gallery with her sister-in-law, Nur Shira.
The inquest began on Sept 3, 2025, to establish the cause and circumstances leading to Zara Qairina's death, including whether any criminal elements were involved.

Title: Maran durian orchard operator loses RM202,460 in lottery scam
Article:
KUANTAN: A 63-year-old durian orchard operator from Bandar Jengka, Maran, lost RM202,460 in a lottery scam after dipping into her savings and pawning her jewellery in an attempt to claim a purported RM1.2 million prize.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the scam began on Nov 25 last year when the victim came across a Facebook video featuring a monk from southern Thailand who purportedly offered financial fortune-telling services.
"The victim contacted the suspect, who advised her to buy a lottery ticket for a chance to win the grand prize.
"She was then told to contact an agent from Kelantan to make the necessary payments. The agent later informed her that she had won RM1.2 million," he said in a statement today.
Azry said the agent demanded payments purportedly for bank processing fees and cross-border transfer taxes before releasing the winnings.
The victim made 12 transactions totalling RM202,460 to six bank accounts between Dec 23 last year and May 22 this year.
She received no winnings and lodged a police report after realising she had been cheated.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
Azry advised the public to be wary of lottery offers, lucky-number predictions and promises of lucrative prizes on social media.

Title: Riyadh airport to remain shut until Oct 17 after deadly Houthi attacks
Article:
RIYADH:  Authorities have extended the closure of Riyadh's international airport until Saturday and airlines scrapped flights after continuing attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis emptied the skies over Saudi Arabia's capital.
Operations at King Khalid International Airport, Saudi Arabia's second-busiest airport after Jeddah, were suspended to "allow for the completion of procedures to ensure the safety and operational readiness of the airport's facilities", the Saudi civil aviation authority said in a statement.
Late on Monday, the Houthis said they had attacked the airport with a ballistic missile, shortly after Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the group towards Riyadh.
The Houthis also said in a statement that they targeted an airbase in Khamis Mushait in the kingdom's southwest with a drone. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation.
A Notice to Airmen issued on Monday showed that the King Khalid International Airport will stay closed until 2100 GMT on Oct 17.
The airport has been shut since an attack on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. On Sunday, another attack killed one person and injured nearly a dozen others.
The attacks marked one of the most significant disruptions to Saudi aviation in years, adding to pressures on an industry already grappling with conflict across the Middle East and with higher jet fuel prices that are eating into profits.
They have also raised worries over civil aviation becoming a target in armed conflict.
"This level of sustained intense attack on civil aviation is unprecedented," said Mark Zee, founder of OPSGROUP, a membership-based organisation that provides aviation safety advice.
"I think this requires us to rethink how we view the current risk picture, and tread very carefully," he said.
Air traffic tracker Flightradar24 showed planes avoiding the city on Monday, though jets were crossing Saudi airspace and landing at top hub Jeddah on the country's west coast.
Cancellations across all Saudi airports reached 46.4pct, aviation analytics firm Cirium said.
CRISIS OVERSHADOWS SAUDI BUSINESS OUTLOOK
The disruption has forced airlines across Europe and Asia to suspend services, while the Federal Aviation Administration advised US carriers on Sunday to exercise caution when flying to or over Saudi Arabia. EU aviation body EASA widened a Saudi airspace warning on Friday, citing missile and drone attacks.
"The impact goes beyond Saudi Arabia to the wider region and to its global connections," said aviation analyst John Strickland.
OPSGROUP advised airlines to avoid the southern aviation corridor over the Middle East altogether, and take a route from Europe to Asia over central Asia.
That adds "extensive distance" for some routes and "closes off options for getting into Dubai, Abu Dhabi for most western carriers," Zee said.
Lufthansa Group has cancelled all flights to Riyadh until Oct 16, while Air France-KLM has extended a suspension to and from Riyadh until the end of the month. Abu Dhabi's Etihad Airways also extended cancellations.
Delta Air Lines said it was delaying planned services from Atlanta to Riyadh, initially due to start on Oct 23, until March 2027.
The escalation with the Houthis has raised concerns over the broader economic impact. Saudi Arabia's real GDP is projected to contract by 3.6pct this year, reflecting a combination of factors including lower oil activity.
The attacks have put events scheduled in Riyadh this month under pressure, including the kingdom's flagship investment conference and the WPC Energy Congress, where several top oil executives were dropped from the programme.--REUTERS

Title: IJM shares fall despite securing RM1.23 bln contruction contract in Kedah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IJM Corporation Bhd shares fell in early trading today despite its unit securing a RM1.23 billion construction contract in Kedah.
At 10.32 am, the counter lost three sen to RM2.77, with 4.405 million shares transacted.
IJM's wholly-owned subsidiary, IJM Construction Sdn Bhd, has accepted a letter of award from AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd for a design and build contract worth about RM1.23 billion.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said it views the contract win as a breakthrough for IJM in the semiconductor buildout space.
"While IJM is no stranger to the E&E sector, this marks its maiden billion-ringgit semiconductor contract as a main contractor. We estimate the project to yield a high single-digit profit before tax margin, with its fast-tracked 14-month construction timeline expected to accelerate earnings recognition in the financial year 2027-2028 (FY2027-28)," it said in a research note.
Meanwhile, RHB Investment Bank noted IJM now has a balance order book of RM10.6 billion, of which around 55 to 60 per cent are from Malaysia.
"From Malaysia's outstanding orderbook, we project around 60 to 70 per cent to come from industrial-related projects, including data centres.  For year-to-date FY2027, IJM has secured RM3.0 billion worth of new jobs versus the group's internal FY27 job win target of RM 6 to 8 billion," it said, adding that it is maintaining its 'buy' call for IJM at a target price of RM3.50.

Title: Bar Council tightens rules on lawyers handling clients' money
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Stricter rules will be imposed on law firms next year when handling clients' money following concerns over dishonest lawyers who have led to substantial insurance payouts.
The Bar Council said the new requirements, introduced under Clause 11(e) of the insurance policy, were aimed at preventing the misuse of clients' funds and protecting their interests.
Under the new rules, law firms with more than one partner must get approval from two partners before making transactions involving clients' accounts.
Firms using online banking must also introduce additional security checks and ensure that the person preparing payment is not the same person approving it.
The changes are part of the Bar Council's 2027 Professional Indemnity Insurance (PII) scheme, which provides insurance protection to law firms against certain claims arising from their legal work.
In a circular dated Sept 25, the council said a significant portion of insurance payouts was due to misconduct and dishonesty involving clients' money.
It warned that if the problem continued, insurance companies would have to pay out more claims, which could eventually lead to higher insurance premiums for all law firms.
"A significant portion of current claim payouts under the PII scheme arises from misconduct and dishonesty related to clients' accounts.
"This trend is unsustainable, as substantial payouts of this nature will inevitably result in higher overall losses and, over time, increased premiums for all firms," it said.
The council said these measures would make it harder for individuals to misuse clients' money without being detected.
Law firms must also continue to comply with the Solicitors' Account Rules 1990 and the Accountant's Report Rules 1990.
The council acknowledged that many law firms already had similar security measures in place but said the new requirements would ensure more consistent practices across the legal profession.
Apart from the new rules, the council also announced changes to insurance coverage for law firms next year.
Firms with one to five lawyers will have their minimum insurance coverage increased to RM500,000, compared with the previous range of RM250,000 to RM450,000.
Firms with six to 35 lawyers will receive an additional RM50,000 in coverage, while larger firms with 36 lawyers or more will benefit from lower amounts they must pay themselves when making an insurance claim.

Title: Eco Discovery 2026 promotes Hulu Selangor's heritage, ecotourism
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Hulu Selangor Explorace: Eco Discovery 2026, held on Oct 10, drew an encouraging response from participants by focusing on ecotourism, environmental sustainability and social responsibility.
Organised by the Hulu Selangor Municipal Council (MPHS) in collaboration with Excapt Event, the event marked the council's fifth anniversary as a municipality and aimed to showcase the district's heritage and tourist attractions.
MPHS president Julaihah Jamaludin said the positive response to the competition, held in Kuala Kubu Bharu, indicated strong public interest in exploring the district's unique history, heritage and natural beauty.
"This also reflects growing interest in visiting Hulu Selangor to discover its unique history, heritage, natural beauty and other attractions," she said in a statement today.
Julaihah said the race's appeal was evident from the participation of 30 teams and continued public demand to take part even after the registration quota had been reached.
She said Kuala Kubu Bharu was chosen for its historic character and Garden City urban planning concept.
"Participants had the opportunity to discover Kuala Kubu Bharu not just as a town, but as a destination rich in history, heritage and its distinct identity," she said.
Julaihah said the explorace challenged participants' agility and teamwork, showcased Kuala Kubu Bharu's history and identity, and promoted environmental sustainability by collecting used cooking oil and electrical and electronic waste (e-waste).
She said participants collected 230kg of used cooking oil and 37 e-waste items weighing a total of 14.65kg through the activities.
As part of the programme's corporate social responsibility initiative, participants also contributed to Pertubuhan Kebajikan Ar Rahmaniah and Asrama Baitul Rahmaniah Bairah, Julaihah said.
"MPHS hopes programmes like this will encourage the public to appreciate local heritage, adopt environmentally friendly lifestyles and support community initiatives to create a more sustainable environment and a thriving community," she added.

Title: Kelantan teacher claims trial over student's death, injury to another
Article:
KOTA BARU: A female teacher has claimed trial in the magistrate's court to two counts of negligence resulting in the death of one student and injuries to another at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tanjong Mas in April.
The accused, Sakinah Ismail, 57, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read before magistrate Wan Mohd I'zzat Wan Abdullah.
According to the first charge, Sakinah is accused of acting negligently while driving her Honda HR-V, causing the death of a 13-year-old girl on the afternoon of April 12.
She was charged under Section 304A of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum two-year jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
For the second charge, Sakinah is accused of negligently knocking down another 13-year-old girl, endangering her life, at the same time and place.
The charge was framed under Section 336 of the Penal Code, which provides for up to three months' jail, a fine of up to RM500, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Nadzir Abdullah prosecuted, while lawyers Muhammad Hasif Hasan and Wan Fadhil Fayyadh Wan Mohd Zuhairi represented Sakinah.
Earlier, Nadzir proposed bail of RM3,000 for both charges with one surety.
Hasif sought a lower amount, saying his client, a religious teacher, had cooperated with the authorities.
He added that she had no prior criminal record and had received the Excellent Service Award twice.
"She was also named the teacher with the best personality at the school last year and is set to retire on Nov 16," he said.
The court set bail at RM2,000 for both charges with one surety and fixed Dec 6 for re-mention.

Title: Malaysia travellers gain new gateways to Europe and Central Asia via Vietjet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian travellers will have more options to explore Europe and Central Asia as Vietjet expands its international network with new routes linking Hanoi to Almaty in Kazakhstan and Prague in the Czech Republic.
The new services mark the airline's expansion into the European Union and strengthen air connectivity between Asia and Europe, with Malaysian passengers able to connect through Hanoi via Vietjet's direct flights from Kuala Lumpur.
The routes will operate twice weekly, on Tuesdays and Saturdays, using Airbus A330 wide-body aircraft. Passengers can opt for Business and SkyBoss services, which offer enhanced onboard hospitality and dining options.
Vietjet chief executive officer Nguyen Thanh Son said the new routes marked an important milestone in the airline's international expansion.
"Vietjet will continue to expand its services to Europe, making travel between Europe, Australia and Asia more convenient," he said.
Prague is known for its historic architecture and cultural heritage, while Almaty, Kazakhstan's largest city, is recognised for its natural landscapes and position as a gateway to Central Asia.
Vietjet currently operates direct flights from Kuala Lumpur to Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Da Nang.

Title: Steel prices climb 5.1pct, cement surges 7.4pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rising steel and cement prices are adding to construction cost pressures, with cement recording an annual increase of up to 7.4 per cent in September.
Steel prices climbed as much as 5.1 per cent in selected areas, according to the Statistics Department.
The department said the steel unit price index rose between 0.1 per cent and 5.1 per cent year-on-year (YoY), with Perak recording the steepest increase at 5.1 per cent, followed by Johor at 4.8 per cent and Tawau at 3.8 per cent.
"The cement unit price index increased by between 0.6 per cent and 7.4 per cent nationwide," it said in its latest special release on building and structural works.
Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negri Sembilan recorded the highest annual increase in cement prices at 7.4 per cent, followed by Kuching at seven per cent and Miri at 6.6 per cent.
However, monthly movements presented a more mixed picture, with some building materials easing in price.
On a month-on-month (MoM) basis, the cement unit price index rose between 0.3 per cent and 1.9 per cent in selected areas in September.
The steepest increase was recorded in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negri Sembilan at 1.9 per cent, while Kota Kinabalu and Kuching registered increases of 0.3 per cent.
In contrast, the sand unit price index fell by 0.7 per cent in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan, and by 0.5 per cent in Perak and Johor.
Steel prices also retreated month-on-month, with the unit price index declining between 0.2 per cent and 1.6 per cent across selected areas.
Johor recorded the sharpest drop at 1.6 per cent, followed by Sibu and Miri at 1.3 per cent.
The average price of Ordinary Portland cement remained unchanged at RM25.80 per bag in September.
The average price of steel, comprising mild steel round bars and Mycon 60 high-tensile deformed bars, fell 2.4 per cent to RM3,431.90 per tonne from RM3,484.20 in August.
The contrasting price movements suggest that while some construction material costs have moderated monthly, cement and steel prices remain higher than a year ago in several areas.
Building material prices are closely watched by developers and contractors because they influence construction budgets, project margins and the cost of delivering new homes and commercial properties.
Persistent cost increases can complicate project planning, particularly for developments operating on tight margins.
The latest figures come amid complaints from developers and contractors that rising input costs are squeezing margins.
Industry groups have warned that broad national price indices may not fully reflect expenses incurred on the ground.
The Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association Malaysia reportedly said in September that 81 per cent of surveyed developers experienced higher business costs in the first half of 2026, up from 74 per cent in the second half of 2025.
Construction costs had risen by an average of about 13 per cent.
Earthworks and infrastructure costs jumped 20 to 30 per cent, although increases for conventional building works ranged between three and five per cent.
The department also reported that the building cost index incorporating steel bars declined month-on-month across building categories, easing by between 0.1 per cent and 1.3 per cent in Peninsular Malaysia.
In Sabah, the index fell between 0.1 per cent and 0.7 per cent across all building categories, while Sarawak recorded declines ranging from 0.1 per cent to 0.5 per cent.

Title: IJM's RM1.23bil Kulim deal signals breakthrough in semiconductor manufacturing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IJM Corp Bhd's RM1.23 billion contract to build a semiconductor manufacturing facility in Kulim marks a breakthrough in its advanced manufacturing business, analysts said.
They expect the fast-track project to support the company's earnings over the next two financial years.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd analyst Brian Chin said the award marked IJM's first billion-ringgit semiconductor plant package as a main contractor, strengthening its position in the nation's semiconductor supply chain.
He said IJM's in-house industrialised building system (IBS) capabilities likely played a key role in securing the contract, given the project's tight 14-month construction timeline.
The contract was awarded to IJM Construction, a wholly-owned subsidiary of IJM, by Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd (AT&S Malaysia).
The project at Kulim Hi-Tech Park, Kedah, involves the design and construction of a four-storey production building, a three-storey central utility building, a wastewater treatment facility and associated infrastructure.
Construction is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026 and be completed within 14 months.
Chin estimated the project would generate a high-single-digit profit-before-tax margin, with the accelerated construction schedule expected to bring forward earnings recognition in the financial years ending March 2027 and 2028.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on IJM with an unchanged target price of RM3.40, while keeping the earnings forecast as
Public Investment Bank Bhd analyst Denny Oh said the award would increase IJM's estimated outstanding order book by 8.5 per cent to RM15.7 billion, including its share of associates.
He estimated the project could contribute about seven per cent to IJM's net profit over the financial year 2027 and 2028 (FY27-28) period, assuming high single-digit margins.
However, Oh left earnings forecasts unchanged, as the contract was already within the firm's RM8 billion order-book replenishment assumption for FY27.
Public Investment Bank reiterated its "Outperform" call on IJM with an unchanged target price of RM3.40.
RHB Research analyst Adam Mohamed Rahim also maintained a "Buy" call and RM3.50 target price, estimating a profit-before-tax margin of between five and eight per cent for the project.
He said the award reinforced IJM's exposure to industrial construction in the northern region, where the group had secured other projects involving semiconductor facilities, automated storage and retrieval systems and medical device manufacturing.
These included an RM455 million automated storage and retrieval system warehouse for a multinational technology company's semiconductor facility in Kulim and an RM454.5 million medical device manufacturing facility for Intuitive Surgical Malaysia in Batu Kawan, Penang.
Adam estimated that industrial-related projects, including data centres, accounted for 60 to 70 per cent of IJM's Malaysian outstanding order book.
He added that potential infrastructure awards, including the Penang Light Rail Transit project, could provide further catalysts for a valuation rerating.
RHB Research kept its earnings forecasts, as the latest award was within its FY27 job replenishment target of RM7 billion.
Despite the positive outlook, the analysts' unchanged earnings forecasts indicate that the contract is broadly in line with expectations rather than an immediate catalyst for earnings upgrades.
The project nevertheless strengthens IJM's track record in complex industrial facilities as demand for semiconductor manufacturing capacity and advanced technology infrastructure expands in Malaysia.

Title: Gang using Mercedes-Benz to steal TM cables in broad daylight busted
Article:
SEREMBAN: A cable theft gang active in four states and recently filmed stealing Telekom Malaysia cables in broad daylight using a Mercedes-Benz and a pickup truck has been busted.
This follows the arrest of 14 people, including two women, after a video of the suspects in action near a primary school in Kampung Melayu Panchor on Oct 9 went viral.
The suspects, aged between 22 and 67, were arrested in a series of raids in Labu, Nilai and Dengkil, Selangor, and have been remanded.
Seremban police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Yatim Osman said the arrests had helped solve several cable theft cases in Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kedah and Melaka.
"We also seized five vehicles, cable-cutting tools, three sacks of burnt copper wire and clothes worn by the suspects during the theft in Panchor," he said.
In the viral incident, four masked men using four vehicles, including a Mercedes-Benz and a pickup truck, were seen pulling cables from two TM manholes near a junction outside the school.
"The case is being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code for theft and Section 235 of the Communications and Multimedia Act."
The offences carry jail terms and fines.
Those with information are urged to contact the Seremban police headquarters at 06-6033222.

Title: IMF upgrades 2026 growth forecast but warns of 'split' outlook
Article:
BANGKOK: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday forecast that global growth in 2026 would slow less than previously expected due to advanced economies' "resilience" in the face of war-fuelled energy prices but warned that low-income countries remained vulnerable to the supply shock.
In its World Economic Outlook (WEO) released at the organisation's Annual Meetings in Bangkok, the Fund raised its 2026 global growth forecast by 0.1 percentage points to 3.1 per cent, compared to 3.5 per cent growth in 2025.
The IMF warned that while many advanced economies have been buoyed by rising investment in artificial intelligence (AI) technology, poorer countries that are not benefiting from that boom face stark choices as they deal with high energy prices due to the US war on Iran.
"The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is under strain, with risks to growth tilted to the downside," said Silvana Tenreyro, the IMF's chief economist.
- 'Bifurcated outlook' -
The United States' war on Iran, launched in February, has plunged the Middle East into violence and seen global energy prices skyrocket as a result of Tehran's retaliatory actions.
Prices of refined petroleum products remain between 70 and 95 per cent above pre-war levels, putting pressure on countries dependent on energy imports for economic activity.
The war is in its eighth month, and Tenreyro warned that "a prolonged conflict in the Middle East could put additional pressures on inflation and slow down growth."
Energy-importing countries not exposed to the AI boom remain the most vulnerable, creating what the IMF termed a "bifurcated outlook" in its WEO report.
The report detailed that the twin economic forces of the war in Iran and the AI technology boom had created a "fragmented" world economy.
"Headwinds from a prolonged war and persistent geopolitical tensions could revive inflationary pressures, strain fiscal and external positions, and hit energy-importing and low-income countries hardest," it said.
"At the same time, the current technology tailwind could stop abruptly if expectations about AI-related profits and productivity gains are reassessed, weakening investment and tightening financial conditions."
- Contraction here, growth there –
The IMF's split view of the world economy was evident in its specific projections.
The Middle East and Central Asia region, exposed directly to the Iran war as Tehran has targeted Washington's Gulf allies, saw the IMF forecast economic contraction of 0.3 per cent in 2026.
Saudi Arabia saw one of the sharpest falls in projected growth, with the IMF forecasting a contraction of 3.3 per cent – a cut in the forecast of 5.0 percentage points.
The IMF said the region is expected to bounce back quickly once the war is over, but there remains high uncertainty as to when that will be.
In advanced economies, growth fuelled by the AI boom and other factors remained strong.
The world's advanced economies were forecast to grow by 2.1 per cent in 2026, with those in the AI supply chain such as Taiwan and South Korea posting significantly higher figures.
Growth in China, the world's second-largest economy, was expected to slow by 0.5 percentage points to 4.5 per cent this year, the IMF said, mainly due to weak domestic demand.
Global inflation remained set to accelerate to 4.7 per cent in 2026, fuelled by the Iran war and the AI boom, with effects spread across both advanced and developing economies.
- 'Urgent action' -
IMF Chief Economist Tenreyro warned that "urgent action" was required by all countries in the face of downside risks.
On the fiscal side, she called on governments to only use temporary and targeted measures to help ease the burden on the public of high energy and other costs.
In lockstep, "monetary policy should remain firmly focused on price stability," she added, indicating that interest rate hikes to curb high inflation were appropriate.
"The economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits," she said. "The task ahead is to move from coping to rebuilding, restoring fiscal space, and rebuilding supply-side resilience."

Title: French school shooting: Teenager fires four shots, wounds two teachers
Article:
AUBAGNE: A 14-year-old boy opened fire with a hunting gun at a middle school in France on Monday, wounding the headmaster and a teacher before being disarmed by a member of staff, local authorities said.
The shooting took place at Joseph-Lakanal middle school in the southern town of Aubagne, near Marseille, where a third person was grazed by gunfire, police said.
Authorities said there did not appear to be a link with high school protests that have rocked France in recent weeks.
"The middle school was not affected by the high school students' protest," police told AFP.
The suspect "came in carrying a bag which was a guitar case. He clearly removed a weapon from this guitar case – a long gun," said Marseille's deputy public prosecutor Audrey Jouaneton.
He fired at least four shots, including inside a classroom occupied by teachers and pupils, leaving a mark on a blackboard, she added.
The headmaster, 53, and teacher, 37, were not in critical condition, according to authorities.
"The suspect, for reasons as yet unknown, fired at the headteacher, who was hit by a shower of pellets in the thighs and lower back," said Jacques Witkowski, prefect of the wider Bouches-du-Rhone region.
He then fired at a second teacher, who was hit by buckshot in the thigh before a member of staff disarmed him, he said.
The suspect "is not known for any history of delinquency or radicalisation," Witkowski added.
Sarah, a pupil at the school, told AFP she heard the fire alarm go off during her Spanish lesson and went into the corridor, where she and her classmates "bumped into" the gunman.
"He started shooting and said: 'I've only come for the teachers, not for the pupils,'" she said.
An investigation into attempted murder has been opened.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, who visited the scene, said the suspect's parents had been taken into custody.
Investigators were "trying to understand how this young person ended up in a position with this gun", Nunez told reporters.
-'PREVENT THE WORST'-
French President Emmanuel Macron on X praised the teaching staff for their quick reaction.
"I commend the composure and exemplary response of the teaching staff, which helped to prevent the worst from happening," he said.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray, who also went to the scene on Monday, called for action against such violence.
"All this seems to sit within a global social phenomenon," he said. "We have to provide a societal response... Schools can't do everything, schools cannot treat major violence."
There has been a spate of violent incidents at French schools in recent months, prompting bag checks on entry in some establishments.
In February, a 14-year-old stabbed an art teacher in southern France at least three times, leaving the 60-year-old in critical condition.
A 14-year-old student in June last year fatally stabbed a teaching assistant in eastern France.
In another, a student carried out a stabbing spree in several classrooms in April last year, wounding a girl and three other pupils. --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's fiscal deficit to narrow, but spending risks persist: BMI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BMI has maintained its forecast for Malaysia's fiscal deficit to narrow to 3.4 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027 from an estimated 3.6 per cent in 2026.
The Fitch Solutions unit said it expects the government to attain its 2027 revenue target of RM380.8 billion, a 4.7 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) increase from the upward revised 2026 target of RM363.3 billion.
"We anticipate that revenue collections will benefit from a favourable growth backdrop.
"The Ministry of Finance had revised higher its 2026 growth projections to 4.8-5.3 per cent (BMI: 5.1 per cent) from 4.0-5.0 per cent previously. It expects growth to moderate to 4.25.2 per cent in 2027 (BMI: 4.5 per cent)," BMI said in a statement.
It further said resilient economic activity should support sales and service tax collections, which have risen from around 7.5 per cent of total revenue in 2009 to 18.0 per cent by the first half (H1) 2026.
Meanwhile, higher oil prices are expected to boost Malaysia's petroleum-related revenue, supported by its position as a net energy exporter.
The government expects dividends from Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) to increase to RM32 billion in 2027 from an estimated RM27 billion in 2026.
"While this suggests that petroleum-related revenue will probably inch higher from 2.5 per cent of GDP in 2026 to 2.6 per cent in 2027, the broader downtrend in Malaysia's reliance on petroleum-related income remains intact," it said.
Operating expenditure is expected to remain high, accounting for 82 per cent of total expenditure, driven by higher subsidies and social assistance, including RM16 billion in cash assistance for low-income households and a rise in the minimum wage to RM2,000 from RM1,700.
The allocation for subsidies and social assistance was raised to RM74.5 billion, or 3.2 per cent of GDP, from the original RM49 billion, amid higher energy costs.
Although spending is expected to ease to RM72.7 billion in 2027, prolonged US-Iran conflict could increase subsidy spending further.
Meanwhile, the development expenditure is set to fall for the third consecutive year to RM83 billion in 2027 (3.6 per cent of GDP), below the RM86 billion annual average implied by the government's RM430 billion commitment through 2030.
BMI said lower development spending could weigh on Malaysia's longer-term productivity and innovation goals, while severe El Niño conditions could prompt additional subsidies for the agricultural sector.
On Oct 9, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled Budget 2027, which totals RM459.8 billion in expenditure — a 3.6 per cent y-o-y increase from Budget 2026.
The government has targeted a deficit of 3.3 per cent of GDP in 2027, marking a gradual pace of consolidation from the revised 2026 target of 3.6 per cent and 3.5 per cent previously, it added.

Title: Kinergy's RM47.5mil data centre contract to add RM1.4mil to net profit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kinergy Advancement Bhd's RM47.5 million data centre contract is expected to contribute RM1.4 million to its net profit over the financial years ending 2026 (FY26) to FY28, said RHB Research.
The research firm said the contract involves core and shell electrical infrastructure works for a data centre, with Kinergy Advancement expected to commence work by year-end and complete the project in the first quarter (Q1) of 2028.
"Assuming a three per cent margin, we estimate that the project will contribute RM1.4 million net profit over FY26 to FY28, with the bulk of recognition in FY27.
"Hence, we expect the job to make up two per cent and one per cent of our FY27 to FY28 earnings, respectively," the firm said in a note.
With the latest win, RHB Research estimated that the Kinergy Advancement has an outstanding order book of RM1.1 billion, which should sustain the company's revenue for 2.5 years.
The research house maintained its "Buy" call on the stock with a target price of 60 sen, noting that the contract falls within its RM60 million new orderbook replenishment target for the engineering division.
"As the award is within our RM60 million new orderbook replenishment target for the engineering division, we make no changes to our numbers.
"We also do not discount it, securing more data centre-related jobs in the future," it added.

Title: Body wrapped in cloth found in Permatang Pauh market drain
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: A man's body, wrapped in cloth, was found in a drain at Sama Gagah Market here around 7am.
A regular visitor, who wished to be identified only as Asma, said she was buying fish when she noticed people gathering near the drain and went to see what had happened.
"I was really shocked to learn that a body had been found.
"In more than 10 years of coming to this market, I have never encountered anything like this," she said.
Asma said she could not get a closer look at the body as police had cordoned off the area to facilitate investigations.
Police had yet to issue a statement on the discovery as of press time.

Title: Johor property back in focus as JS-SEZ plan, RTS lift investor confidence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor's property market is poised for a defining moment, with the highly anticipated Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) masterplan and blueprint set to be unveiled this December.
RHB Research said the move could unlock fresh value across Iskandar Malaysia and reinforce the region's position as a premier cross-border investment hub.
The unveiling, confirmed at the 2027 Budget, is scheduled to coincide with the annual Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat, placing the economic zone firmly in the spotlight as both countries deepen bilateral economic cooperation.
The launch will be officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, signalling high-level commitment to the JS-SEZ and its role in driving investment, economic growth and longer-term property demand in Johor.
The rollout will introduce 12 targeted strategic initiatives alongside broad non‑fiscal policy support, designed to cement JS‑SEZ's standing as a leading regional destination for trade, industry, and real estate growth.
RTS DELAY: A BRIEF PAUSE, NOT A SETBACK
RHB Research analyst Loong Kok Wen underscored that the delay to the much-awaited Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link should be viewed as a temporary setback rather than a derailment of the project's long-term growth potential.
While the RTS link will see its public opening pushed back by one to two months to February 2027, the delay reflects rigorous final safety assessments by independent consultants and regulatory approvals from Malaysia's Land Public Transport Agency and Singapore's Land Transport Authority, steps to ensure long‑term reliability.
"Despite the delay, the investment thesis for Iskandar Malaysia has not changed," Loong said in a recent note.
She added that despite the adjustment to the timeline, the core investment thesis for Iskandar Malaysia remains fully intact.
TOP PLAYS POISED TO DELIVER
Loong said leading developers and industrial‑focused property groups are already seeing strong market momentum, with demand driven by cross‑border connectivity, industrial expansion, and new township growth.
Eco World Development Group Bhd (EcoWorld) stands out with exceptional take‑up across its industrial portfolio.
Loong said Eco Business Parks I, II and III, plus the high‑tech Quantum Edge development, have drawn robust interest from local and international manufacturers, industrial operators, and fast‑growing data centre investors, positioning Johor as a digital and advanced manufacturing hub.
KSL Holdings Bhd has also demonstrated sharp buyer appetite with its Riveria Garden township, launched earlier in 2026 and already fully sold, underscoring enduring demand for well‑located, large‑scale residential communities.
Meanwhile, Loong said Mah Sing Group Bhd is gearing up to introduce MS Industrial Park @ Kulai in late 2026 or early 2027, tapping into surging demand for modern industrial space near key transport links.
UEM Sunrise Bhd, Sunway Bhd and other key Iskandar Malaysia players also remain well‑placed to capture sustained value growth as JS‑SEZ policies and infrastructure roll out, she said.
WHAT THIS MEANS FOR INVESTORS
With the masterplan now weeks away, policy frameworks taking shape, and the RTS link on the horizon, Johor is moving beyond promise to delivery.
For homebuyers, industrial tenants, and investors alike, this is far more than a single infrastructure project, it is the building of a shared economic zone that will tie Malaysia and Singapore closer together for decades to come.
The fundamentals have not shifted The region's long‑term appeal, amplified by policy backing, cross‑border integration, and diversified growth, continues to strengthen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK shoppers stay cautious as fuel costs bite
Article:
LONDON: British consumers kept a lid on spending in September, with much of their extra outlay going on fuel, while warm weather helped pubs but hurt clothing sales, according to surveys published on Tuesday.
The British Retail Consortium (BRC) trade body said its total retail sales measure rose by 1.3 per cent compared with a year ago, picking up from 0.7 per cent in August but below its 12-month average of 1.5 per cent.
A separate survey from Barclays, based on consumer card spending data, showed a 2.0 per cent annual increase in September, slowing from August's 2.1 per cent rise.
It pointed to a rise in households' confidence around their finances but also some nerves ahead of Finance Minister John Healey's budget on October 28.
Here are the key points from the two surveys:
• The BRC said food sales were up by 2.5 per cent while non-food sales edged up by 0.3 per cent.
• Health and beauty had its strongest month of the year so far and toys were boosted by Pokemon's 30th anniversary products, but clothing and footwear had a weak month due to unseasonably warm weather.
• "Retail sales growth remained subdued in September as households are still cautious with their spending ahead of expected rises in household bills and taxes," said BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson.
• Barclays said essential spending was up by 2.5 per cent, driven by a 17.3 per cent jump in fuel spending after diesel prices hit record highs, while non-essential spending edged up by 1.8 per cent.
• Bars, pubs and clubs reported a 3.8 per cent rise in spending, their fourth straight month of growth, as summer weather extended through most of September
• Barclays' measure of confidence in household finances rose to a seven-month high of 67 per cent, but 68 per cent of consumers said they were concerned about the budget's impact on their finances and 30 per cent said they were cutting back on non-essential spending.
• The BRC survey covered the period of Aug 30-Oct 3, while the Barclays spending data was Aug 22-Sept 24
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rusting away: Over 27,000 abandoned vehicles in Klang Valley
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rows of cars left for months, and even years, along roadsides and in housing areas are not only an eyesore but have also become a persistent problem for residents, prompting calls for firm action by local authorities.
Three local authorities in the Klang Valley recorded a total of 27,117 abandoned vehicles, based on records covering different periods from 2021 to August this year.
Kajang Municipal Council recorded the highest number at 12,290 vehicles, followed by Kuala Lumpur City Hall with 11,001 complaints and Ampang Jaya Municipal Council with 3,826 vehicles.
Vehicles left for too long not only take up parking spaces and obstruct road users but could also pose safety risks and affect the cleanliness of their surroundings.
Abandoned vehicles can pollute soil and water through oil leaks and become breeding grounds for mosquitoes and pests.
Local authorities face difficulties removing abandoned vehicles due to problems tracing owners, inaccurate registration details and lengthy verification and disposal processes.
High repair costs and vehicles that are no longer economical to use are among the factors driving owners to abandon them.
This raises questions about the effectiveness of efforts to tackle the problem more comprehensively.
Kajang Municipal Council recorded 12,290 abandoned vehicles of various types, with the figure showing an upward trend from 2021 to August this year.
Over the past three years, the council received 3,351 complaints related to abandoned vehicles: 1,016 in 2024, 1,216 last year and 1,119 this year.
A council spokesman said Cheras subdistrict recorded the highest number of complaints of abandoned vehicles, particularly in housing areas and around car workshops, with old cars being the most commonly abandoned vehicles.
"Among the factors identified are damaged vehicles, high vehicle repair costs, owning more than one vehicle and vehicles sold without a change of ownership.
"The council will conduct an on-site investigation within 14 days of receiving a complaint, and a warning notice will be affixed to the vehicle.
"Owners are given 14 days to remove the vehicle before towing action is taken," the spokesman said in a written statement to Harian Metro.
According to the council, 2,605 vehicles have been towed, while another 9,685 cases remain unresolved.
The spokesman said the council's main challenges included vehicle owners who had changed addresses, missing vehicle registration numbers and original owners who had sold vehicles without transferring ownership to the new owners.
"Kajang Municipal Council does not bear any towing costs for abandoned vehicles, as it appoints the Car Medic panel to tow vehicles whose notice period has expired, in the presence of enforcement officers," he said.
He said abandoned vehicles also obstructed traffic and visibility, increasing the risk of accidents.
The spokesman said leaking oil and other fluids from abandoned vehicles could pollute soil and water, affect cleanliness and tarnish the area's image.
"The vehicles also have the potential to become breeding grounds for disease vectors and nesting places for pests, as well as depriving the public of parking bays," the spokesman said.
To address the problem, the council will appoint contractors to facilitate towing. It will also raise awareness among vehicle owners and publicise information on assistance with vehicle disposal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget will boost digital ecosystem
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget reinforces Malaysia's commitment to strengthening its digital economy through investments in connectivity, artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and analysts say.
The initiatives aim to expand digital access, improve public services and boost economic competitiveness. However, analysts say effective implementation, domestic  technology development and private sector participation will be crucial to achieving these goals.
Among the key initiatives are RM5 billion for the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA), RM1 billion for the national digital healthcare ecosystem and RM142 million to strengthen National Information Dissemination Centres (NADI).
The JENDELA allocation will expand high-quality Internet coverage in rural and remote areas, including Orang Asli villages. It will also improve connectivity along 7,000km of roads and highways, and 1,700km of rail routes nationwide.
The National Digital Healthcare Ecosystem and Connectivity Initiative (PERSADA) will improve digital infrastructure and connectivity in the healthcare sector. It will support the expansion of Electronic Medical Records, telehealth services and drone deliveries of medicines to improve access to healthcare in rural and remote areas.
The NADI allocation will strengthen its role as a digital community hub by providing training in digital skills and AI, while supporting local economic development and entrepreneurship.
The Madani Submarine Cable System (SALAM) will increase network capacity and resilience between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. WiFi at public higher education institutions and a Sovereign AI Cloud are also expected to improve connectivity and strengthen data sovereignty.
MCMC will intensify its Safe Internet Campaign in schools nationwide and continue efforts to combat digital fraud. These include blocking more than 5.7 billion scam-related calls and short message service messages.
MCMC said the initiatives would help ensure digital investments deliver tangible benefits to the people, industry and country.
Nusantara Academy for Strategic Research senior fellow Prof Azmi Hassan said the government's commitment was clearer when allocations across ministries and digital infrastructure projects were considered together, rather than focusing solely on the Digital Ministry's RM1.36 billion allocation.
"The government has shown its commitment through the combined allocations for ministries, education, infrastructure and AI to ensure Malaysia does not fall too far behind in the digital economy," he told
Business Times
.
Azmi welcomed the additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions, saying these could widen access to technology and improve young people's employability.
He said the RM142 million allocation for NADI could help small and medium enterprises explore new opportunities through its online business platform.
However, he said the initiatives' success should be measured by the number of jobs created and the foreign direct investment attracted to AI and other digital industries.
Institute of Strategic and International Studies Malaysia chairman Datuk Prof Dr Mohd Faiz Abdullah said the next challenge was ensuring businesses translated access to digital technology into productivity gains.
[[nid:1554161]]
He said Malaysia needed to develop homegrown solutions that could compete internationally, with stronger support for domestically developed software and AI, start-ups, research and development, and talent development.
Faiz said AI adoption varied across sectors. Financial services were moving towards scaling up their strategies, while manufacturers remained largely at the experimentation stage.
Malaysia's ambition to establish 3,000 smart factories by 2030 remained a significant challenge, with only 93 having completed their transformation.
"Unless there is a massive acceleration in the build-up rate, this will set Malaysia back from the vision of realising dark factories which can function 24/7 without explicit human supervision," he said.
Faiz said Malaysia could build on its existing strengths in data centre construction, cooling systems and telecommunications, developing expertise that could be exported to other countries.
Other opportunities included advanced semiconductor packaging and AI applications in healthcare and agriculture.
He said connectivity investments would be more effective if rural communities had reliable electricity and fast Internet access.
He cited Sabah as an example of how energy constraints, slow Internet and limited economic opportunities could hinder digital transformation.
Faiz proposed state-by-state assessments of innovation, research and development, productivity and exports to identify bottlenecks and ensure digital initiatives addressed local needs.
National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) chief executive Dr Megat Zuhairy Megat Tajuddin said the  2027 vsupported efforts to strengthen Malaysia's technological sovereignty and prepare critical systems for emerging cyber threats.
"Ultimately, resilience requires more than adopting technologies developed elsewhere. We must harness our domestic talents, researchers and industry players to develop, test and deploy solutions that address national security needs," he said.
He said the collaboration between NACSA and MCMC would support the development of home-grown data protection technologies against quantum threats, alongside efforts to strengthen CSCDC Bhd.
Malaysia's National Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration Plan 2025–2030 and AI Systems Cyber Security Framework would help prepare critical systems for emerging risks.
Megat Zuhairy said cybersecurity progress should be measured through stronger protection of critical infrastructure and personal information, faster incident responses and more reliable digital services.
An AI-powered scam-checking application could  prevent financial losses, he said. However, it would need to be backed  by intelligence-sharing, coordinated investigations and cross-border enforcement cooperation.
International Islamic University Malaysia professor of Asean studies and political science Dr Phar Kim Beng said Malaysia's digital transformation required effective execution and greater private-sector participation, given its limited fiscal room.
[[nid:1554160]]
"Malaysia has a small budget to make any digital quantum leap," he said, stressing the need for public-private partnerships and safeguards against corruption and leakages.
Phar said Malaysia should strengthen its position in regional submarine cable infrastructure, with Selangor potentially becoming a hub supported by bunkering services for cable-laying vessels.
He called for stronger regional cooperation involving China, Japan, South Korea and Asean nations to combat cross-border online scams.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Over 25,000 foreigners detained in crackdown on illegal businesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department conducted 12,343 operations against businesses illegally run by foreigners from 2024 to Sept 30 this year, resulting in the detention of 25,124 foreigners, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said the operations comprised Op Belanja, targeting business and retail premises; Op Jaja, focusing on hawker activities; and Op Selera, targeting restaurants, eateries and food preparation premises.
He said 5,173 operations were conducted under Op Belanja, involving inspections of 20,882 people, with a total of 5,809 undocumented migrants and 471 employers detained.
For Op Jaja, 567 operations were carried out, involving inspections of 8,473 people. These resulted in the detention of 734 undocumented migrants and 40 employers.
Meanwhile, 6,603 Op Selera operations were conducted, involving inspections of 51,847 people. A total of 19,301 undocumented migrants and 1,341 employers were detained.
Saifuddin said action was taken under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Immigration Regulations 1963 against foreigners found staying or working illegally in the country.
"Common offences included not possessing a valid pass or permit, overstaying and violating the conditions of a pass or permit.
"Those convicted could face fines or imprisonment. Foreigners ordered to be deported would be placed at immigration depots while documentation and travel documents were arranged with their respective embassies or diplomatic representatives before being sent home," he said in a parliamentary written reply.
On allegations that syndicates or other parties were protecting illegal business activities, Saifuddin said all information and complaints received would be examined through intelligence gathering and further investigations.
He said the department would continue intelligence-led and targeted enforcement operations through Op Belanja, Op Jaja and Op Selera to curb the abuse of immigration facilities by foreigners.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fury as US federal agents search anti-Trump lawmaker's home
Article:
WASHINGTON: US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of what officials said was a criminal investigation, marking a dramatic escalation in President Donald Trump's confrontation with the outspoken lawmaker.
Omar said she was "ok" following the operation but accused the administration of targeting political opponents just three weeks before she seeks re-election in the Nov 3 midterms.
The early morning search – described by Trump's "border czar" Tom Homan as part of a longstanding probe – was conducted by agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US immigration enforcement.
"Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponise federal law enforcement," Omar wrote on X.
"For 10 years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation."
The operation also sparked a furious backlash from Democrats who accused Trump of abusing government powers to pursue his political opponents.
Fox News reported that the search was linked to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration paperwork submitted on behalf of the Somali-born congresswoman by her late father when she was a child.
[[nid:1554150]]
The president was asked about Omar hours after the operation and said she was being investigated "very carefully."
"I've always found her to be totally crooked personally, but that has nothing to do with me. I think she's a terrible person, just a complainer. She comes from a country that is a non-country," he told reporters at the White House.
The Justice Department confirmed in a statement Monday that agents had carried out a "judicially authorised search warrant" in the Washington area, but officials did not identify Omar or disclose the nature of the probe.
"This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation," prosecutors added.
Omar, 44, is a leftist Democrat and fierce critic of Trump, particularly his administration's sweeping crackdown on immigration.
The Republican president has repeatedly clashed with Omar, who came to the United States from Somalia as a child and has frequently been the target of his political attacks.
Top House Democrat Hakeem Jeffries and his leadership team called the search "deeply disturbing" and raised questions about "the continued corrupt weaponisation of the federal government against Donald Trump's adversaries."
Minnesota's Democratic Governor Tim Walz accused Trump of "abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election."
[[nid:1554149]]
Republican congresswoman Nancy Mace, meanwhile, said Omar should be stripped of her US citizenship and deported if fraud was proven.
"NO ONE is above the law," she wrote on X.
The timing also drew criticism from Xochitl Hinojosa, a former director of public affairs at the Justice Department.
"There's a longstanding rule at DOJ that you don't take overt actions like this before an election, especially when there's a candidate on the ballot," she wrote on X.
Omar said in September that Homeland Security officials had not contacted her about any investigation, dismissing the allegations against her as politically motivated attacks.
Omar was first elected to Congress in 2018 and represents a district including Minneapolis, home to one of the largest Somali communities in the United States.
She is a member of the group of left-wing Democratic lawmakers known as "The Squad," who have been among Trump's most vocal opponents in Congress.
No charges against Omar were announced in connection with Monday's search.
