Title: Australia business confidence falls further in September amid oil price volatility
Article:
SYDNEY: Australian business conditions were broadly unchanged in September, though confidence slipped further amid a surge in oil prices driven by renewed tensions in the Middle East, raising concerns over higher costs, a survey showed on Tuesday.
The survey from National Australia Bank showed its index of business conditions was flat at -1 in September. However, the ongoing decline in confidence suggests that conditions will likely deteriorate further, the survey said.
Confidence fell 4 points to -13, well below the level recorded in February, before the US-Israeli conflict with Iran began.
"Energy prices remain elevated, funding costs have risen and domestic growth has slowed in 2026," NAB said.
"Against this backdrop, it is not surprising that both business confidence and business conditions are well below their respective long-run averages."
Over the month, business confidence fell in five out of eight industries. Mining, wholesale and retail saw "some improvement" in sentiment, though in trend terms, confidence remains negative across all industries except mining, NAB said.
Global oil prices experienced extreme volatility in September after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis launched missile and drone strikes against Saudi Arabia. The conflict, now a spillover of the broader US-Iran tensions, has driven oil prices higher, fuelling fears of persistent inflation.
The Reserve Bank of Australia last month raised its cash rate to a 15-year high of 4.60 per cent - its fourth hike of the year - and warned it may have to tighten further to curb inflation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: 19 areas nationwide record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nineteen areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 180.
Johor was the worst-affected state, with eight areas recording unhealthy readings, according to the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System.
The other affected areas in Johor were Larkin (176), Kota Tinggi (169), Pengerang (166), Batu Pahat (161), Kluang (154), Tangkak (151) and Segamat (133).
In Sarawak, Sri Aman recorded an API reading of 172, followed by Serian (154) and Samarahan (129).
In Pahang, unhealthy readings were recorded in Balok Baru, Kuantan (161) and Rompin (157).
In Melaka, Bukit Rambai and Bandaraya Melaka each recorded 160, while Alor Gajah registered 151.
In Negri Sembilan, Seremban recorded 154 and Nilai 146, while Tawau in Sabah recorded 154.
Putrajaya recorded the highest moderate reading at 99, followed by Kemaman, Terengganu (98) and Kapit, Sarawak (97).
In the Klang Valley, Johan Setia recorded 90, Klang 87, Batu Muda 82, Cheras 81 and Shah Alam 81.
Four areas recorded good air quality: Taiping, Perak (49); Balik Pulau, Penang (43); Jerantut, Pahang (36); and Langkawi, Kedah (27).
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said yesterday that schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan and Putrajaya
would be closed
today due to the haze.
An API reading of zero to 50 is categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy and above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC probes viral video over allegedly false, misleading Budget 2027 tax claims
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is examining a viral video alleged to contain false and misleading information regarding the Sales and Service Tax (SST) and income tax relief in the 2027 Budget.
The MCMC said it has received public complaints regarding the video, which has been circulating on social media.
According to the statement, the dissemination of such information could cause confusion regarding national taxation policies, trigger unfounded concerns, and influence the public’s financial decisions based on incorrect information.
“In this regard, MCMC has referred the matter to the Ministry of Finance and is currently assessing the video’s content, including the context of its dissemination and its potential impact on the public.
“Further action will be considered if there are violations of prevailing laws, including Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 [Act 588],” the statement read.
The MCMC also emphasised that freedom of speech must be exercised responsibly and should not be abused to spread false information that could harm the public interest.
Meanwhile, the public is urged to verify information related to the 2027 Budget through the Ministry of Finance’s official portal at
www.belanjawan.mof.gov.my
, the
Sebenarnya.my
portal, the AIFA chatbot via WhatsApp at 03-8688 7997, and the official channels of relevant authorities before believing or sharing such information. — Bernama

Title: Police seek witnesses, dashcam footage after fatal Cheras-Kajang crash that killed motorcyclist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Police are appealing to witnesses to a fatal accident involving a motorcycle and a lorry at KM13.1 of the Cheras-Kajang Highway yesterday, which claimed the life of a 23-year-old male motorcyclist.
Kajang police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said a report on the accident was received at about 6pm.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim, who was riding from Kuala Lumpur towards Kajang, is believed to have lost control before falling onto the road.
“At the same time, a lorry that was moving straight ahead could not avoid the victim in time and ran over him, causing his death at the scene,” he said in a statement today.
He said the lorry driver has yet to lodge a police report.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for driving recklessly or dangerously, causing death.
He urged witnesses or anyone with information to come forward and assist the investigation, including members of the public with dashcam footage or video of the accident.
“They can contact the investigating officer, Insp Nur Faezah Mohd Zakria, at 012-326 8496,” he said.
He also advised road users to always be responsible and prudent, comply with the rules and prescribed speed limits, and drive with care. — Bernama

Title: Pasir Gudang logs country’s worst air quality at 181 API, 20 stations remain unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Air quality across Malaysia showed modest improvement this morning, with 20 of the country's 68 monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10.40am, down from 23 stations reported yesterday afternoon.
According to Department of Environment (DOE) surveillance data, 44 stations recorded moderate air quality, four registered good levels, and none breached the very unhealthy or hazardous thresholds. Readings between 101 and 200 fall within the unhealthy classification.
Johor continued to bear the brunt of the transboundary smoke, accounting for eight of the nation's unhealthy monitoring stations.
Pasir Gudang logged the highest reading nationwide at 181, climbing from 174 yesterday afternoon. Larkin saw a steep surge, rising from 160 to 176, while Kota Tinggi held steady at 169 and Pengerang remained at 166. Batu Pahat rose to 162, Kluang stood at 153, Tangkak recorded 151, and Segamat re-entered the unhealthy register at 138.
In Sarawak, Sri Aman posted the third-highest reading nationally at 170, up from 153 yesterday. IPD Serian held relatively stable at 154, while Samarahan improved significantly, dropping from 148 to 108 to hover just inside the unhealthy band. In Sabah, Tawau recorded an elevated reading of 155, up from 149.
On the east coast of the peninsula, Pahang had two affected stations, with Balok Baru in Kuantan at 161 and Rompin at 157.
In Melaka, all three monitoring stations remained in the unhealthy range: Bukit Rambai and Bandaraya Melaka were tied at 160, while Alor Gajah recorded 151.
Relief in central corridor and Putrajaya
Encouraging improvements were recorded across the central belt. In Negeri Sembilan, Seremban eased from 167 to 154, while Nilai dropped from 164 to 151. Coastal Port Dickson exited the unhealthy bracket entirely after logging 154 yesterday.
The federal administrative centre of Putrajaya recorded substantial clearing, dropping from 156 to 120, safely below the 150-mark threshold designated for potential localized school closures.
Industrial hotspots Kemaman, Paka, and peat fire zone Johan Setia, which were all unhealthy yesterday, also dropped off the affected list.
The latest readings coincide with widespread school closures in effect today.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek previously announced that all primary and secondary schools across Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, and Putrajaya would suspend physical classes today.
The closures also apply to schools under four District Education Offices (PPD) in Selangor: Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat, and Sepang, alongside PPD Kuantan and PPD Rompin in Pahang. Schools in all other unaffected districts are operating as normal.
Health and education authorities have reiterated advice for parents, high-risk groups, and students with respiratory ailments to wear protective face masks outdoors and track hourly API updates through official channels.

Title: Is Malaysia’s fiscal health on the mend? BMI says yes in post-Budget forecast
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — BMI has maintained its forecast for Malaysia’s fiscal deficit to narrow to 3.4 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027 from an estimated 3.6 per cent in 2026.
The Fitch Solutions unit said it expects the government to attain its 2027 revenue target of RM380.8 billion, a 4.7 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) increase from the upward revised 2026 target of RM363.3 billion.
“We anticipate that revenue collections will benefit from a favourable growth backdrop.
“The Ministry of Finance had revised higher its 2026 growth projections to 4.8-5.3 per cent (BMI: 5.1 per cent) from 4.0-5.0 per cent previously. It expects growth to moderate to 4.2-5.2 per cent in 2027 (BMI: 4.5 per cent),” BMI said in a statement.
It further said resilient economic activity should support sales and service tax collections, which have risen from around 7.5 per cent of total revenue in 2009 to 18.0 per cent by the first half (H1) 2026.
Meanwhile, higher oil prices are expected to boost Malaysia’s petroleum-related revenue, supported by its position as a net energy exporter.
The government expects dividends from Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) to increase to RM32 billion in 2027 from an estimated RM27 billion in 2026.
“While this suggests that petroleum-related revenue will probably inch higher from 2.5 per cent of GDP in 2026 to 2.6 per cent in 2027, the broader downtrend in Malaysia’s reliance on petroleum-related income remains intact,” it said.
Operating expenditure is expected to remain high, accounting for 82 per cent of total expenditure, driven by higher subsidies and social assistance, including RM16 billion in cash assistance for low-income households and a rise in the minimum wage to RM2,000 from RM1,700.
The allocation for subsidies and social assistance was raised to RM74.5 billion, or 3.2 per cent of GDP, from the original RM49 billion, amid higher energy costs.
Although spending is expected to ease to RM72.7 billion in 2027, prolonged US-Iran conflict could increase subsidy spending further.
Meanwhile, the development expenditure is set to fall for the third consecutive year to RM83 billion in 2027 (3.6 per cent of GDP), below the RM86 billion annual average implied by the government’s RM430 billion commitment through 2030.
BMI said lower development spending could weigh on Malaysia’s longer-term productivity and innovation goals, while severe El Niño conditions could prompt additional subsidies for the agricultural sector.
On Oct 9, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled Budget 2027, which totals RM459.8 billion in expenditure – a 3.6 per cent y-o-y increase from Budget 2026.
The government has targeted a deficit of 3.3 per cent of GDP in 2027, marking a gradual pace of consolidation from the revised 2026 target of 3.6 per cent and 3.5 per cent previously, it added. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Myanmar refugees, Gaza crisis, and minimum wage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The implementation of the RM2,000 minimum wage from June 2027, the registration of Myanmar refugees, and measures to address the humanitarian crisis in Gaza are among the key issues scheduled for discussion in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official portal, during the Minister’s Question Time (MQT), Aminolhuda Hassan (PH-Sri Gading) will ask the Economy Minister to explain government mechanisms to ensure the minimum wage implementation does not result in job losses, price hikes, or increased operating costs for small enterprises.
Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau) will ask the Home Minister about the target for registering Myanmar refugees over the next two years through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) Programme, including targeted numbers and implementation timeline.
Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik) will ask the Foreign Minister to outline the government’s strategic steps following three years of genocide in Gaza, particularly in strengthening protection for Palestinians, humanitarian aid access, international accountability, and the reconstruction of Gaza.
During the oral question-and-answer session, Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man (PN-Kubang Kerian) will ask the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister about the expected new net generation capacity operating by 2030 and the capacity committed through Power Supply Agreements with data centres.
Ahmad Johnie Zawawi (GPS-Igan) will ask the Education Minister about the number of reserve teacher candidates among Sarawakians awaiting appointment, teaching vacancies according to options, and plans to absorb them.
Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa (BN-Tampin) will ask the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister for an update on a study to enact specific legislation against ticket scalping, including existing legal loopholes that hinder enforcement.
Following the question-and-answer session, the house will continue debating the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage, following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, last Friday.
According to the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 will run from Oct 12 to 22, followed by a four-day ministerial winding-up session starting Oct 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sits for 37 days until Dec 8. — Bernama

Title: RM510b but no new taxes? Amir Hamzah says 20227 Budget possible through cutting leakages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The government is confident it can spend the RM510 billion allocated in Budget 2027 without introducing any new taxes, says Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said the government has always emphasised governance to reduce leakage and wastage in the current system to improve the efficiency of national spending.
“The government’s approach is to ensure that what we spend is money well spent to improve the country’s economy and for the people’s benefit.
“When we have focus and carry out our responsibilities well, the government and the country will be more successful in the future,” he said in the Bicara Naratif program aired on RTM 1 titled “Budget 2027: Reaching For The Skies, While Anchored on Our Values,” yesterday.
Amir Hamzah said the country’s continuously strengthening economic data reflects the confidence of foreign investors to keep investing in Malaysia, which in turn can generate national income.
“But the most important thing is ensuring that when the revenue is there, we spend wisely, we close the gaps for any leakages that occur, and we increase the returns we get more efficiently in government expenditure, and this will be tied to the introduction of several new laws,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Unregistered Orang Asli in Malaysia: Why the NRD struggles to find accurate numbers
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 13 — The absence of accurate numbers of individuals without identification documents poses a challenge for the National Registration Department (NRD) in identifying the Orang Asli and indigenous communities who are still left out of the national registration system.
NRD director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias said that his department can only identify these individuals when they come forward to seek JPN services, making it difficult to determine the actual number of those who still do not have identity cards or birth certificates.
He said the issue not only involves the Orang Asli community in Peninsular Malaysia but also the indigenous communities in Sabah and Sarawak, who are believed to still have individuals without identification documents.
“We do not know exactly how many are unregistered, nor do we know how many will attend; however, Alhamdulillah, we have received applications from more than 30 individuals aged 12,” he said at a press conference following the Registration Literacy Programme, held in conjunction with the state-level 78th National Registration Day celebrations, in Pos Balar here yesterday.
He said that NRD is committed to implementing outreach programmes to engage with communities in rural areas, including providing services for first-time identity card applications, identity card replacements, as well as matters related to birth and death certificates.
Badrul Hisham said that continuous efforts are important to ensure that communities in rural areas have access to documentation services, as well as to help address the issue of registration neglect among those communities.
Meanwhile, during the programme, more than 30 Orang Asli children aged 12 in Pos Balar here applied for their identity cards for the first time through the JPN outreach programme today.
Badrul Hisham said that the response to the documentation services provided through the NRD mobile van has been very encouraging, with the local community also taking the opportunity to obtain identity card and birth certificate replacement services.
He said the number of first-time MyKad applications for 12-year-old children is expected to increase as many residents were still queuing to obtain NRD services during the programme.
“For today, we have received more than 30 who are getting their ICs for the first time (12 years old). And if we look at the mobile van, there were still many people queuing,” he said.
He said that the Menyemai Kasih Rakyat (Mekar) programme is part of NRD’s commitment to reach out to communities in rural areas to facilitate their access to identity documents.
In addition to first-time MyKad applications, he said NRD also provides services for replacing identity cards as well as handling matters related to birth and death certificates.
The effort is important to ensure that communities in rural areas have easier access to the registration and documentation services provided by the government. — Bernama

Title: Man feared drowned after being swept away in Kajang’s Sungai Chuah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — A local man in his 40s is feared drowned after being reportedly swept away in Sungai Chuah, Kajang, Sunday.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the search and rescue (SAR) operation, which began yesterday, was suspended at 4.30 pm yesterday due to heavy rain and will resume tomorrow.
He said the search was carried out using kayaks and boats, alongside search efforts along the riverbanks.
"The department's K9 tracker dog unit and Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel are also involved in locating the victim at the scene," he said in a statement.
JBPM received an emergency call at 5.23 pm yesterday regarding a local man who was swept away in the river before disappearing from view.
The Kajang Fire and Rescue Station dispatched a team that arrived at the scene, located about four kilometres from the station, at 5.29 pm, before the search operation was expanded with assistance from the Shah Alam and Port Klang stations. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia aims to slap ‘disaster’ status on transboundary haze at Asean meet
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 13 — Malaysia will raise the issue of transboundary haze at an Asean foreign ministers’ meeting ahead of the bloc’s 49th Summit in Manila, the Philippines, next month to discuss more effective regional mechanisms to tackle the problem.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the haze issue required special attention as it was not covered by existing Asean mechanisms for natural disasters.
“We already have an Asean mechanism for natural disasters, but haze is not included or classified as a natural disaster.
“So, this will be one of the issues that I will personally raise at the meeting with my counterparts,” he told reporters after attending the departure of Jordan’s King Abdullah II at the Bunga Raya Complex here yesterday.
On the latest efforts to extinguish fires in Indonesia, he said his counterpart, Arrmanatha Nasir, had informed him that extremely poor visibility in affected areas was hampering aerial firefighting operations.
“Indonesia has between three to four aeroplanes and 34 helicopters, but they cannot take off because visibility is so poor that it is unsafe for any flights in the affected areas.
“However, they have deployed 60,000 people to work on the ground,” Mohamad said, adding that Indonesia also faced challenges because the fires were located deep inland, water supplies were limited and fires continued to smoulder in peatland areas.
He said cloud-seeding operations could not be carried out in Indonesia at present because suitable cumulonimbus clouds were absent.
Mohamad said Malaysia acknowledged that the Indonesian government was doing its utmost to extinguish the fires and sympathised with the situation facing the country.
However, he said Malaysia hoped its neighbour would take more effective measures as the current situation was adversely affecting the public. — Bernama

Title: MOH will push for absorbing contract dental and pharmacy officers, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will recommend absorbing contract dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions for the consideration of the Ministry of Finance and the Cabinet, in an effort to ensure the future and welfare of these groups are safeguarded.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal would be pursued within a reasonable timeframe, based on the approach previously used to address the issue of contract medical doctors.
“...the first step will be followed by other service schemes, namely dentists and pharmacists as well,” he said when met after appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme titled ‘Realising Budget 2027 With the Health Minister’ last night.
He said the recruitment of dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions would utilise a new quota separate from the 9,000 permanent medical doctor positions announced under Budget 2027.
The Malaysian Dental Association (MDA) was previously reported to have urged the government and MOH to consider permanent appointments for contract dental officers, following the announcement of permanent appointments for medical doctors.
Commenting on reports regarding dental officers whose contracts ended without being renewed, Dzulkefly said MOH would continue to pay attention to their welfare and work experience within the public healthcare system.
In another development, Dzulkefly expressed hope that the Ministry of Finance would consider a request for a seed allocation of approximately RM100 million to strengthen non-communicable disease (NCD) management at the primary healthcare level.
He said the allocation is crucial to enhancing prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, and continuous control of chronic diseases such as diabetes and high blood pressure.
“Matters related to NCD management are a major component I am bringing into the reforms. In addition to PeKa B40, which received an allocation of RM80 million, managing NCDs from a healthcare perspective is essential to effectively address this chronic disease pandemic.
“It encompasses not only first-stage screening, but also continuous diagnosis, treatment, and control for conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure,” he said.
He added that benchmarking per capita expenditure for NCD management also takes into account practices in countries like Singapore and Indonesia, as well as global trends prioritising primary healthcare services. — Bernama

Title: Pack of eight stray dogs attacks child at Johor playground; Iskandar Puteri council launches raid
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 13 — A seven-year-old boy was injured after being attacked by a pack of six to eight stray dogs while playing at a playground near a low-cost housing flat in Lima Kedai here yesterday.
Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad said the incident occurred between 3 pm and 4 pm, when the boy was believed to have been playing before the stray dogs attacked him, causing him to fall and roll on the ground as he tried to escape.
“Fortunately, a man who witnessed the incident threw stones at the dogs from a distance, helping to save the boy.
“I was informed of the incident by the village head and went to the flats to inspect the location,” he told Bernama when contacted.
He said the victim sustained injuries to the eye area, neck, head and body and was rushed to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Bahru for treatment.
Pandak said such incidents are deeply concerning and require immediate action by the authorities.
He said the incident was not the first of its kind in the area, as a 15-year-old boy had also been attacked by a pack of eight stray dogs at about 6 am the same day.
The teenager managed to drive the animals away before fleeing to the building’s staircase, but sustained injuries to his leg.
Pandak said he had met the teenager and advised him to seek treatment at a nearby clinic, while the seven-year-old boy is receiving treatment at HSA.
He said the matter had been brought to the attention of the local authority and he was informed that the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) would conduct an operation tonight to address the stray dog problem in the area.
He said appropriate action needs to be taken immediately to ensure the residents’ safety, particularly that of children, even if it might draw objections from non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
“How long are we going to allow this to happen? Do we have to wait for someone to die before action is taken?” he said.
He also visited the victim and expressed hope that effective measures would be implemented to prevent similar incidents, particularly in residential areas with public facilities for residents.
In an earlier incident on Sept 5, a two-year-old girl, Nur Haira Wafiqah, was reported to have sustained serious injuries after being attacked by five stray dogs in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat.
The victim suffered serious injuries to several parts of her body in the attack. — Bernama

Title: Deputy minister warns ‘influencers’ against exploiting religious rituals for content
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Social media influencers have been reminded not to exploit issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R), particularly religious rituals, for online content, in the interest of preserving harmony in the country’s multiracial society.
Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said influencers with large followings should be more responsible in producing content and spreading positive values instead of playing on 3R sentiments.
"If possible, stay away from issues involving 3R, as influencers may not know about the religious rituals or customs of certain communities, especially if they do not profess that religion.
"We have many positive things that can be promoted together with the National Unity Ministry,” he said when met after attending Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme at Wisma Bernama yesterday.
He was commenting on a viral issue involving an influencer believed to have participated in a religious ceremony during the Thaipusam celebration at Batu Caves, Selangor.
Yuneswaran said the ministry viewed the issue involving religious rituals seriously and hoped it would be handled tactfully, adding that the investigation had been left entirely to the religious authorities and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
He also urged the public not to rush to judgement or politicise the issue, but to allow the authorities to conduct their investigation and resolve the matter promptly.
In addition, he invited social media influencers to work with the ministry to promote the Federal Constitution, the Rukun Negara and the National Nationhood Programme.
"Under the ministry, we recommend that these issues (3R) be avoided. Although our society comprises people of various races and ethnic groups, we can attend various ceremonies, events and celebrations; however, when rituals are involved, I hope they will be respected,” he said.
On Sunday, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) confirmed that it had begun investigating a viral post involving an individual believed to be Muslim who was alleged to have participated in another religion’s ritual in contravention of Islamic law. — Bernama

Title: Higher minimum wage not a silver bullet, but crucial for income growth, says Johan Merican
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The implementation of the RM2,000 minimum wage next June is structured to provide businesses and corporations with an adequate transition window to adjust their salary frameworks, Treasury Secretary-General Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said.
Speaking to reporters following the Post-Budget 2027 Debate organised by the Malaysian Economic Association in Kuala Lumpur yesterday, Johan identified sluggish wage growth relative to living expenses as the primary driver of household financial strain, even as headline inflation remains contained.
“This is why driving up the people's earning power is so critical. Raising the minimum wage is part of that strategy.
“While it isn't a silver bullet on its own, it plays a vital role and we are starting with large companies,” Johan said.
Johan said that the broader policy goal extends beyond lifting wages for entry-level workers to preventing wage compression, an outcome where pay raises for the lowest tier inadvertently squeeze differentials while intermediate salaries remain stagnant.
“The hope is that these large companies will also look at their overall salary structures and make adjustments based on the increase in the minimum wage.
“This is why the government mandated that government-linked-companies (GLC) adopt a living wage baseline of RM3,400, setting a benchmark for the private sector to follow when determining salary levels,” he said.
Johan noted that the RM2,000 baseline was deliberated and endorsed without contention by the National Wages Consultative Council, which comprises representatives from both trade unions and employer federations.
Extended adjustment window for small businesses
However, the Cabinet decided to grant an extended adjustment grace period for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to buffer them against operational cost shocks while they navigate the economic spillover effects of ongoing Middle East geopolitical tensions.
Alongside the RM2,000 statutory minimum wage and the RM3,400 GLC living wage threshold, Johan said the government will also maintain momentum on the Progressive Wage Policy, with plans also underway to introduce a dedicated minimum wage tier for semi-skilled occupations.

Title: Malaysia is getting a new e-commerce law, what could change for online shoppers?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Online shoppers could see clearer accountability for e-commerce platforms and sellers under a new law.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced when tabling Budget 2027 that the government had agreed to introduce a new law to replace Malaysia’s Electronic Commerce Act 2006.
If passed by Parliament and brought into force, the proposed legislation would strengthen accountability among online platforms and sellers.
Alongside this move, the government is also examining legislative and enforcement measures to protect local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from unfair competition and ensure products bought by consumers are safe.
The move follows the government’s decision to repeal and replace the 2006 Act, which Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said did not comprehensively define the responsibilities of platforms, sellers and other participants in online transactions.
On September 19, Armizan said the ministry had approved the policy decision to replace the existing law with a more comprehensive framework.
What does the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 not adequately cover?
The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living’s (KPDN) through their review of Malaysia’s e-commerce regulatory framework, published in October 2025 had identified gaps in platform accountability and the wider regulatory framework.
There are several areas that the 2006 Act does not adequately address.
Regulating e-commerce platforms directly
The Act does not provide a comprehensive framework governing how online marketplaces must operate or what regulatory obligations they must fulfil.
Clearly defining platform accountability
It does not comprehensively establish the responsibilities of platforms when sellers engage in misleading or potentially harmful practices.
Regulating sellers and their conduct
The Act does not comprehensively regulate online sellers and their businesses.
Addressing cross-border e-commerce
The existing framework does not adequately address regulatory and enforcement challenges posed by overseas sellers and platforms serving Malaysian consumers.
Platform oversight and enforcement
There is no comprehensive legal framework addressing oversight of platforms and ensuring accountability.
Keeping pace with the wider digital marketplace
The Act does not adequately define the roles and responsibilities of intermediaries involved in product visibility, advertising, transactions and access to consumers.
So, what could change for people who shop online?
The Electronic Commerce Act 2006 primarily provides legal recognition for electronic transactions.
A new law could give shoppers greater clarity over a marketplace’s responsibilities when a seller offers misleading products, fails to fulfil an order or engages in questionable practices.
Will platforms have to do more to ensure products are safe?
Product safety is one of the concerns highlighted by the government.
In his Budget 2027 speech, Anwar said the government was examining legislative and enforcement measures to ensure goods bought by consumers were safe.
The government has also raised concerns about foreign e-commerce companies operating in the Malaysian market without adequate oversight. The proposed law is intended to examine a broader framework for regulating platforms and sellers.
Will it become easier to identify a seller?
Identifying the actual seller can be difficult when consumers make purchases through large online marketplaces, particularly when businesses operate from overseas.
KPDN’s review of the e-commerce regulatory framework considered stronger seller identification and information-disclosure requirements, including measures to help establish the identity of businesses operating online.
Such measures could help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions and give authorities better information when investigating complaints.
What if the seller is based overseas?
Cross-border transactions can complicate enforcement when a seller has no registered business entity in Malaysia.
Consumers who receive defective products, do not receive their orders or have disputes over transactions may find it difficult to pursue the seller, particularly if the business operates in another country.
The government has identified the regulation of foreign e-commerce businesses as an area requiring attention.
Armizan has also highlighted regulatory gaps affecting foreign sellers and said the government was studying ways to strengthen platform accountability and the application of Malaysian laws to overseas entities.
Will it be easier to resolve disputes and obtain refunds?
KPDN’s findings identified dispute resolution and consumer redress as areas requiring improvement, including the possibility of a more integrated online dispute-resolution mechanism.
In February, Armizan told Parliament that the ministry was considering a more comprehensive online dispute-resolution platform that could handle the process from filing a complaint to adjudication or a decision.
Such a system could make it easier for consumers to submit complaints and pursue disputes digitally.
Will online marketplaces need a licence?
Licensing is another regulatory option being considered to strengthen oversight of e-commerce platforms.
On September 19, Armizan had in a Bernama report said the government was studying the possibility of introducing a licensing regime, particularly in view of overseas goods entering the market, consumer safety and the sustainability of local MSMEs.
The distinction matters because registration, licensing and other compliance requirements can impose different obligations on businesses.
What happens next?
In his Budget 2027 speech, Anwar announced that the proposed e-commerce Bill would likely be tabled at the next Parliament sitting in March to strengthen accountability among online platforms and sellers.
The Bill’s detailed provisions will determine how far the reforms go, including whether they introduce new obligations for platforms, strengthen oversight of foreign sellers or create additional avenues for consumer redress.
Until the replacement law takes effect, existing legislation — including the Consumer Protection Act 1999 and the Consumer Protection (Electronic Trade Transactions) Regulations 2024 — continues to apply where relevant.

Title: Firefly cancels Subang-Singapore flights until October 14 as haze persists
Article:
SINGAPORE, Oct 12 — Prevailing weather and haze conditions have forced Firefly to extend flight cancellations between Subang and Singapore’s Seletar Airport until October 14, with affected passengers being offered alternative Malaysia Airlines flights, subject to seat availability, or full refunds.
Firefly, a wholly owned subsidiary of Malaysia Airlines, had earlier cancelled all scheduled flights between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport from October 10 to 12 as a precautionary safety measure.
In an advisory on Monday, the airline said the extended cancellations involved six daily services: FY3122 and FY3123, FY3124 and FY3125, FY3126 and FY3127, FY3128 and FY3129, FY3130 and FY3131, as well as FY3132 and FY3133.
“Affected passengers are being contacted and reallocated onto available Malaysia Airlines services via the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore route, subject to seat availability.
“Passengers who opt not to proceed with the reallocated flights are eligible for a full refund, which will be credited back to the original payment method within 30 working days,” it said.
Meanwhile, Singapore’s air quality remained unhealthy on Monday, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) ranging from 118 to 155 as of 7 pm, according to the National Environment Agency (NEA).
Readings stood at 155 in the central and west regions, 139 in the east, 122 in the south and 118 in the north. — Bernama

Title: Federal-state cooperation key to inclusive, sustainable development, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Close cooperation between the federal and state governments is essential to ensuring that national development is planned in an inclusive, sustainable and comprehensive manner for the benefit of the people.
In a Facebook post, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he made the remarks while chairing the 51st National Physical Planning Council (MPFN) meeting in Putrajaya today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the meeting reviewed various matters related to national physical development, including land-use planning and State Structure Plans, in line with the Town and Country Planning Act 1976 (Act 172).
“All relevant parties must continue to improve service delivery to strengthen the investment ecosystem and make dealings easier for the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kedah police: Motorcycle theft allegation believed to have led to teen’s torture death
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 12 — An allegation that an 18-year-old youth had stolen a motorcycle is believed to have prompted a group of suspects to torture him before his body was found by the roadside in Jalan Harvard, Gurun, last Thursday.
Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said police received information about the discovery of the body at 8.05am on October 8, while a post-mortem found that the victim had died from blunt force trauma to the head.
He said the suspects were believed to have acted out of anger after receiving complaints from local residents that the victim had stolen a motorcycle.
“The victim was caught in Pendang on October 5 before being taken to the house of one of the suspects, where he was detained for two days, tortured and beaten, and had his hair cut,” he told reporters at the Kedah Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
Adzli said the victim was found dead inside the house on the night of October 7, and his body was subsequently dumped by the roadside.
He said police arrested 14 men aged between 16 and 24 in operations around Gurun and Guar Chempedak from noon to 8.30pm on October 8, a few hours after the body was discovered.
Police seized 14 mobile phones, a Honda City, scissors and the victim’s identity card. Twelve suspects have been remanded for six days until Wednesday, while two underage suspects have been remanded until tomorrow. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
The victim, identified as Muhammad Haikal Mohd Shahrilnizam, 18, was found wearing yellow and black sportswear and had injuries to his head and face. He was initially found without identification documents.
In a separate case, Adzli said police were tracking down two men to assist in investigations into an attempted murder and obstructing police officers from carrying out their duties during Ops Pintas, an operation against migrant smuggling at the Hutan Kampung Toll Plaza here on October 7.
He said police had intercepted a Proton X70 SUV suspected of carrying five migrants, but the driver allegedly acted aggressively, attempted to run over a police officer and crashed into the toll barrier.
“Police fired one shot at the tyre, but the suspect fled and abandoned the vehicle in Pendang, about 28.3 kilometres from the scene,” he said.
Adzli said several individuals had been detained, while police were seeking Muhammad Raffi Yusrino, 28, and Zulfikrie Naaim Morhinino, 36, to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry to strengthen oversight of public funds through amended Audit Act, new procurement law
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Finance Ministry will use amendments to the Audit Act 1957 and the Government Procurement Act 2026 to strengthen oversight of public funds and improve transparency in government spending.
Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the amended Audit Act gives the Auditor-General greater scope to trace funds across government agencies and examine how the money is used.
“The government has also approved the Government Procurement Act, which enables the government to tighten oversight in terms of transparency and value for money in the procurement process.
“The Act will be enforced next year, where the government will also share details on companies receiving the contracts,” Johan said.
The Government Procurement Act 2026 was gazetted on May 26 and is expected to come into operation in 2027, subject to a commencement date appointed by the Finance Minister through a gazette notification.
Johan said governance would be further strengthened through a proposed Government-Owned Entities Bill, which is intended to improve oversight of procurement and investment by government-owned entities, including government-linked companies and statutory bodies.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had previously said the proposed Bill was intended to prevent major financial scandals, including 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), and mismanagement involving Tabung Haji and Felda, from recurring.
Separately, Anwar said the Government Procurement Act would improve transparency through the publication of project details, including the names of contractors and contract values, once it comes into force in 2027.
“When governance is corrected, the benefits resulting from the change will contribute to the people’s welfare,” Anwar said previously.

Title: Malaysia targets 3.3pc fiscal deficit in 2027, 3pc by 2028, says Treasury sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Malaysia is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.3 per cent next year as it presses ahead with plans to bring the figure down to 3 per cent by 2028, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said today.
Speaking at a panel discussion titled “Post-Budget 2027 Debate” organised by the Malaysian Economic Association in Kuala Lumpur, Johan said fiscal consolidation remained a key government priority, particularly in maintaining investor confidence.
“This is an area where the government is placing strong emphasis on.
“This is so Malaysia can demonstrate our ability to execute disciplined and prudent financial management.
“As such we remain committed to the pledges made under the Fiscal Responsibility Act — so that we can achieve a fiscal deficit as low as three per cent by 2028,” he said.
The government is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.6 per cent this year, after reducing it from 5.5 per cent in 2022 to 3.7 per cent in 2025.
Johan said uncertainty in the Middle East and the possibility of higher oil prices had been factored into the government's planning for next year.
“Consequently, we estimate that this year’s subsidy allocation of around RM40 billion will be maintained into next year.
“However, just as was practiced this year when oil prices rose higher than anticipated, we will make adjustments according to circumstances,” he said.
The government's fiscal consolidation efforts are guided by the Public Finance and Fiscal Responsibility Act 2023, which provides a framework for responsible management of public finances.

Title: Seven-year-old seriously injured in Johor stray dog attack, teen escapes unhurt in earlier incident at same location
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 12 — A seven-year-old boy suffered serious injuries after he was attacked by eight stray dogs while playing at a playground at a housing complex in Lima Kedai here today.
During the incident, which occurred at 3pm, the primary one pupil suffered injuries to his eyes, neck, head, and body before being rushed to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Bahru for treatment.
Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad expressed concern over the incident urging authorities to address the issue of stray dogs.
“Immediate measures are required to prevent a recurrence of such incidents, particularly those involving children and residents using public facilities within the housing complex,” he said after visiting the victim at his home here today.
Pandak said the incident involving the child was the second to occur today.
He said he was informed that an earlier incident took place at 6am, where an 18-year-old male was attacked by a pack of stray dogs at the same location.
“However, the teenager managed to fend off the animals without sustaining any injuries, he said, adding that the incidents, occurring within a span of just a few hours, have raised concerns regarding the safety of residents, especially children.
Pandak hopes the relevant authorities will take immediate action to ensure the safety of residents in Lima Kedai.
He said an effective plan is needed to resolve the issue of stray dogs.

Title: Govt aims to improve water quality in 33 polluted rivers in Malaysia by 10pc, says DPM Fadillah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The government aims to improve the Water Quality Index (WQI) of 33 rivers identified as polluted in 2025 by at least 10 per cent within a year, with appropriate recognition to be given to state governments that achieve the target.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the target was set at the second 2026 meeting of the National Special Committee on Addressing River Water Quality Deterioration, which he chaired today.
Fadillah, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister, said Department of Environment (DOE) reports showed that the number of polluted rivers rose from 25 in 2023 to 27 in 2024 and 33 in 2025.
In Selangor, the Selangor Water Management Authority (Luas) reported 144 cases of water source pollution detected over the three years up to September 14, 2026, with varying levels of risk.
“I appreciate the commitment of Luas and relevant agencies nationwide in detecting and addressing pollution. However, this increase clearly shows that existing measures need to be strengthened through more effective, coordinated and sustained action,” he said in a Facebook post.
Fadillah said polluted rivers could disrupt water treatment plant operations, affect public water supplies, increase treatment costs and affect economic activities, underscoring the need to make water resource protection a shared priority at all levels of administration.
He said the meeting also decided to conduct a pilot study on the integrated management of non-point source (NPS) pollution at a selected local authority area to test the applicability of field data, estimate pollution loads, identify priority areas and formulate appropriate control measures.
In addition, a Technical Committee on Effluent Discharge Standards, chaired by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government, will be established in collaboration with the National Water Research Institute of Malaysia (NAHRIM) to coordinate the implementation of effluent discharge standards in urban and rural areas.
The meeting also saw the launch of the Guidelines for the Installation of Floating Solar Panels on Water Reservoirs and Lakes in Malaysia, which will serve as a reference to ensure that floating solar developments are carried out in a planned and sustainable manner while safeguarding the country’s water resources.
The integrated efforts reflected the government’s commitment to tackling pollution at its source, protecting water resources and safeguarding national water security through cooperation between the federal government, state governments, local authorities and all stakeholders, he added. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Pet vaccination, sterilisation eligible for tax relief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The government proposes expanding the scope of individual income tax relief for lifestyle to include pet care expenses, such as vaccinations and sterilisation treatments by registered veterinary services.
In the Budget 2027 tax measures document, the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said the expansion would also cover the costs of adopting a rescued pet from a registered animal shelter.
The proposal aims to cultivate kindness and empathy toward animals in need of care.
MoF said the personal income tax relief cap for lifestyle remains at RM2,500, including the proposed expansion.
Additionally, to promote digital literacy and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technology to boost productivity and drive innovation, the scope of the personal income tax relief for lifestyle is proposed to be expanded to include subscription costs for AI software and applications for personal use, spouses, or children.
Currently, beginning with the 2024 assessment year, the personal income tax relief for lifestyle is limited to RM2,500 and covers the purchase of reading materials, including e-books and daily newspapers in print/electronic form, as well as personal computers, smartphones, or tablets, and internet subscriptions. — Bernama

Title: High Court allows MCMC’s preliminary objection, Papagomo committal hearing on Dec 23
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The High Court will first hear the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) committal application against blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, before proceeding with the inter-partes injunction hearing.
MCMC’s counsel, Datuk Selva Mookiah, when confirming the matter said Judge Datuk Dr Arik Sanusi Yeop Johari made the ruling after allowing MCMC’s preliminary objection that the committal application should be heard first, as Wan Azri must purge the contempt first, before proceeding with the inter-partes injunction hearing.
He said the court fixed December 23 to hear both matters.
“The court also extended the existing ad interim injunction against Wan Muhammad Azri until December 23. The committal hearing will determine the allegation of contempt of court, while the inter partes hearing will consider the injunction in the presence of both parties,” he said.
On June 19, the court granted an ex parte interim injunction sought by the MCMC, restraining Wan Muhammad Azri from publishing allegedly defamatory statements against the commission and ordering him to immediately cease publishing and disseminating harmful online content through social media.
The order also prohibits Wan Muhammad Azri from using any social media platform, whether through existing or new accounts, to publish or distribute false, misleading or harmful content.
On August 6, Wan Azri used Facebook and/or YouTube social media platforms to publish and/or cause to be published a live session containing false, misleading and/or harmful online contents, in breach of the ad interim injunction dated July 6.
Therefore, MCMC has applied to the court for leave to commence a committal proceeding against Wan Azri.
On October 6, the court granted MCMC leave to initiate committal proceedings against Wan Muhammad Azri over an alleged breach of the injunction through a live session published on Facebook and/or YouTube on August 6.
On May 27, the MCMC filed the suit, alleging that Wan Muhammad Azri had posted defamatory statements on social media claiming the commission had censored court reports relating to Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil’s case against him.
In its statement of claim, the MCMC said it had never been involved in any form of censorship regarding reports on the Kuala Lumpur High Court proceedings involving Fahmi and the defendant.
The commission maintained that the defendant’s allegations were false, baseless and had undermined public confidence in the regulator. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Jordan seek high-tech cooperation to train more engineers, says Anwar
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Malaysia and Jordan are seeking to expand strategic cooperation in high-tech industries, particularly semiconductors and advanced technical education and training, to develop more engineers and skilled workers for future industry needs.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said these were among the key areas discussed during his meeting today with Jordan’s King Abdullah II, who was on a two-day state visit to the country at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
He said the talks focused on strengthening bilateral ties in higher education, skilled human capital development, emerging technologies and the semiconductor ecosystem.
“We also discussed potential cooperation in developing advanced technical education and training centres, including producing more engineers and skilled workers to meet future industry demands,” he posted on Facebook.
Anwar said discussions also covered expanding trade and investment, including a potential free trade agreement (FTA), tariff restructuring, stronger supply chains and cooperation in energy, transport, the halal industry and tourism.
Anwar said he and King Abdullah also exchanged views on geopolitical developments in West Asia, particularly in Palestine and Syria, and their implications for regional security and stability.
He said they also agreed on the urgent need to end atrocities against Palestinians, including continued violence and rights violations in Jerusalem and the West Bank.
“I stressed that Malaysia will remain steadfast in championing Palestinian rights while strengthening humanitarian assistance, particularly for the people of Gaza,” he said.
Anwar noted that the Jordanian monarch also expressed appreciation for Malaysia’s stance and efforts in supporting the Palestinian cause.
Anwar also expressed hope that the meeting would elevate Malaysia-Jordan relations through closer economic and technological cooperation, as well as shared commitments to humanity, peace and global justice.
The state visit was King Abdullah’s second to Malaysia since May 2008, as both countries marked more than six decades of diplomatic relations established in 1965.
Prior to his departure after concluding the visit, King Abdullah granted Anwar an audience at the Bunga Raya Complex, Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), for about 30 minutes to discuss strengthening longstanding bilateral relations.
Bilateral trade reached RM993.4 million in 2025, up 15.2 per cent from 2024, while trade from January to August 2026 rose eight per cent year-on-year to RM740.7 million. — Bernama

Title: TNB confirms electrical accident at its installation in Johor’s Kota Tinggi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) has confirmed an electrical accident involving a member of the public at one of its installations in Kota Tinggi, Johor, today.
In a statement posted on Facebook by TNB CareLine, the utility company said its technical team was dispatched to the location shortly after receiving a report of the incident.
TNB said the incident was believed to be linked to vandalism and that it would provide full support and cooperation to the authorities in their further investigations.
The company also advised the public against tampering with, opening or approaching electrical installations, warning that such actions could result in serious injury or death.

Title: No need to replace old birth certificates, still valid, says NRD; new copies cost RM5
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 12 — Old birth certificates, including handwritten documents issued in paper format, remain valid and do not need to be replaced, said National Registration Department (NRD) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias.
He said those who wished to obtain a birth certificate in the new format could apply for an extract at any NRD office for RM5, with the process taking less than five minutes.
“Birth certificates are never invalid, whether they are from the older or newer generation,” he told reporters after the Registration Literacy Programme held in conjunction with the Kelantan-level 78th National Registration Day celebration at Pos Balar here today.
Badrul Hisham said birth documentation was essential to establish a legally recognised identity and ensure individuals could access their rights and services as Malaysians.
He said the NRD continued to reach out to communities, including the Orang Asli in rural areas, to ensure they had access to registration and documentation services.
Asked about the number of Orang Asli who had yet to obtain a MyKad or birth certificate, he said the department did not have exact figures, as it could only identify those who came forward to seek its services.
He said awareness efforts on the importance of personal documentation needed to continue through outreach programmes and cooperation with relevant agencies to ensure no one was left out of the national registration system. — Bernama

Title: Kedah police bust online scam syndicate posing as Indian police officers
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 12 — Kedah police successfully crippled an online scam syndicate involving suspects posing as Indian police officers during a raid on a business premises in Bandar Putra, Kulim, last Friday.
Kedah Police Chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said that during the joint operation at 8pm, police arrested 48 individuals suspected of acting as syndicate members, comprising seven locals, eight Indian nationals, and 33 Pakistani nationals.
“This syndicate began operating late last August at a three-story shoplot running online scam activities by impersonating as police officers from India, targeting victims from that country.
“They used the Telegram app to communicate and deceive victims by claiming the victims’ phone numbers were involved in illegal activities. Victims were asked to transfer money into provided bank accounts for police investigation purposes,” he told reporters at the Kedah Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) here today.
He added that investigations into the syndicate members, aged 20 to 43, revealed that they claimed they were duped after applying for jobs offered on social media before being added to a Telegram group and promised salaries of around RM2,500 to RM3,500 a month.
“Investigations also found that the syndicate members failed to present valid travel documents for entry into Malaysia. So far, a total of 73 individuals have fallen victim to this syndicate’s scams, involving losses of nearly RM1.4 million.
“Additionally, police seized various items including 89 mobile phones, seven laptops, modems, monitors, Indian police uniforms, Indian flags, Indian Central Bureau of Investigation flags, and several other items. The total value of the seizures is estimated at RM70,000,” he said.
Adzli further added that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code (PC), Section 120B of the PC, and Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Meanwhile, he noted that follow-up arrests were made at 6:00 pm yesterday involving two local men and three local women aged 44 to 51, who acted as the premises owners, real estate agents, and renters of the involved premises.
“All these arrests were made around Kulim and Tanjung Piandang, Perak, and checks revealed that the five new suspects arrested have no prior criminal records.
“The success of this operation is the result of public information, so the police would like to thank the public for staying alert to their surroundings. If there is any information regarding scam activities, please channel the information to enable prompt action to be taken,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Opposition leader criticises GLC involvement in non-core projects in Budget 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that government-linked corporations (GLCs) were being made to operate beyond their core mandates.
While debating Budget 2027, he cited a project to build a hostel for students that he said would be funded by the Retirement Fund Incorporated (KWAP), alleging this practice extended to others such as Petronas, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and more.
"Too many of them have been used...for example, KWAP's fundamental purpose is to preserve and grow that capital so it can cover future pensions for retirees or those eligible to receive them,” he said during today’s debate.
"So why is the government asking KWAP to go and build student hostels? Where are the financial returns? I am truly bewildered at times."
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for 2027 last Friday, in which he also outlined a RM50 billion from government-linked investment companies, state enterprises and statutory bodies.
Hamzah criticised this today, saying the GLCs should not be involved with industries beyond their own to prevent a loss of focus.

Title: Two killed, two injured in three-vehicle pile-up on Federal Highway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Two men were killed while two others were injured in an accident involving three cars at Kilometer 18.2 of the Federal Highway heading towards Kuala Lumpur, early this morning.
Petaling Jaya District Police Chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said the accident, which occurred at approximately 12.20am, involved a Proton Wira driven by a local man in his 20s who was travelling from Shah Alam to Kuala Lumpur.
He said that preliminary investigations found the driver of the Proton Wira was believed to have failed to control his vehicle before crashing into the road divider on the right side of the highway, triggering a collision with two other cars traveling behind it.
“As a result of the accident, the driver of the Proton Wira and a passenger in his 20s suffered severe injuries and were confirmed dead at the scene.
“Two other passengers, who were friends of the victims, sustained injuries to their bodies,” he said in a statement today.
Shamsudin said the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters received a report regarding the fatal accident at 1:05 am today.
He stated that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
In the meantime, he reminded all road users to always comply with traffic laws to prevent accidents.
“The police will not compromise with road users who do not obey regulations and will take firm action against any road user who violates the law,” he said.
Shamsudin also appealed to witnesses who saw or were at the scene to come forward to the nearest police station or contact the traffic investigating officer, Insp Mohd Nazar Md Kasim, at 012-5653395 to assist with the investigation. — Bernama

Title: 1MDB in talks to settle lawsuit with Deutsche Bank
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) is in talks with Deutsche Bank (Malaysia) Berhad to settle a lawsuit filed against the bank.
1MDB’s counsel, Datuk Lim Chee Wee, informed the Federal Court of the settlement talks during proceedings today before a three-member panel led by Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah.
The panel, comprising Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Seri Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru, was hearing 1MDB’s application for leave to appeal against a decision in favour of UK law firm White & Case LLP.
“We have already informed the High Court that there is a proposed settlement between our client (1MDB) and Deutsche Bank. The hearing for that case is scheduled for October 26 before High Court Judicial Commissioner Rihada Rafie,” Lim said.
However, the terms of the proposed settlement were not disclosed.
On May 7, 2021, 1MDB filed a US$1.83 billion suit against seven defendants, alleging breach of contract, negligence and criminal conspiracy in the misappropriation of its funds.
1MDB named Deutsche Bank (Malaysia) Berhad, Coutts & Co, JP Morgan (Switzerland), Petrosaudi International, Petrosaudi Holdings (Cayman), Tarik Obaid and Patrick Mahony as the first to seventh defendants.
The plaintiff alleged that all the defendants conspired to defraud 1MDB, and provided dishonest assistance causing losses to the company as well as damaging 1MDB’s reputation and good name.
However, on November 13, last year, 1MDB had dropped JPMorgan and Coutts and Co from the suit.
Meanwhile, on 1MDB’s application for leave to appeal to the Federal Court, counsel Datuk Dr Cyrus Das, representing White & Case, told the panel that he objected to 1MDB’s application to include more than 3,000 pages of additional documents in support of its leave application.
Another counsel for 1MDB, Khoo Guan Huat, informed the court that the issue had been raised during case management before the Federal Court last week.
The panel then allowed 1MDB’s application to include the additional documents and directed that affidavits be filed. The court also ordered that case management be held today to fix an early hearing date for the application.
On August 20, this year, the Court of Appeal granted an appeal by White & Case LLP against a High Court decision that allowed a lawsuit filed by 1MDB on alleged fraud to be heard in Malaysia, ruling that the High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear 1MDB’s suit against the firm.
1MDB filed the suit in the Kuala Lumpur High Court in 2024, seeking US$1.83 billion and US$33 million in losses from White & Case and Mahony. The fund alleged that White & Case assisted PetroSaudi in committing fraud and conspired to harm 1MDB while acting as its legal counsel.
Last year, the High Court rejected White & Case’s challenge, ruling that it could hear the lawsuit because the trial witnesses are located in Malaysia. — Bernama
